Title: June unemployment rate remains at 3.0pct, Statistics Department
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The unemployment rate remained unchanged at 3.0 per cent in June 2026, with 517,800 unemployed persons recorded, according to the Labour Force Statistics for June 2026 and the Second Quarter of 2026 released today.
The Statistics Department said the number of employed persons rose 0.01 per cent to 16.83 million in June 2026 (May 2026: 16.82 million persons), while the number of unemployed persons increased from 513,400 to 517,800, rising by 0.9 per cent month-on-month.
"The labour force recorded a marginal month-on-month increase of 0.04 per cent to 17.34 million persons in June 2026 (May 2026: 17.34 million persons). The labour force participation rate (LFPR) remained at 70.9 per cent, unchanged from the previous month," it said in a statement today.
It said the employees' category comprised 75.0 per cent of the total employed persons, increasing slightly by 0.02 per cent, reaching 12.61 million persons in June 2026  (May 2026: 12.61 million persons), while the number of own-account workers rose marginally by 0.04 per cent to register 3.15 million persons (May 2026:  3.15 million persons).
The department said the services sector remained the primary contributor to total employment during the month, particularly in transportation and storage, accommodation and food and beverage service activities, as well as wholesale and retail trade activities.
In June 2026, it added that the unemployment rate among youths aged 15 to 24 years stood at 10.2 per cent, with 292,200 unemployed youths recorded (May 2026:  291,600 persons), while the unemployment rate for those aged 15 to 30 years was unchanged at 6.3 per cent, registering 400,800 unemployed youths.
At the state level, Putrajaya continued to record the lowest unemployment rate at 1.3 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, followed by Melaka and Pahang both at 2.0 per cent and Selangor that representing an unemployment rate of 2.1 per cent, it said.
Concurrently, five states recorded the LFPR above the national rate, with Putrajaya registered the highest rate at 79.4 per cent, followed by Selangor (77.9 per cent) and Kuala Lumpur (76.0 per cent).
"Overall, Malaysia's economic and labour market outlook from July 2026 onwards is expected to remain positive, supported by relatively stable domestic economic conditions, continued investment activity and a labour market that has demonstrated resilience.
"Nevertheless, the prolonged uncertainty surrounding global energy markets, geopolitical developments and external trade conditions could weigh on business costs and hiring decisions if these pressures persist," it added.

Title: King orders comprehensive, transparent probe into TH RCI findings - Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has decreed that investigations into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) be conducted comprehensively and transparently, with no compromise.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the King had instructed that the investigations be conducted "without any compromise, with no stone left unturned".
He said the decree reflected the rulers' concern over safeguarding public trust and upholding the integrity of TH, which manages the pilgrimage funds of millions of Malaysian Muslims.
"I would like to take this opportunity to convey my highest appreciation for His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim's decree, which emphasised that investigations into the findings of the RCI on TH must be conducted comprehensively, transparently and without compromise, leaving no stone unturned," he said during a special sitting of Parliament today to debate the RCI report.
Zulkifli said the decree was in line with the government's commitment to safeguarding the trust placed by TH depositors.
He said the Cabinet had unanimously decided on July 29 to make the RCI report public and have it tabled and debated for the first time in a special parliamentary sitting.
The Cabinet also agreed that full investigations be conducted immediately by the relevant enforcement agencies based on the RCI findings, he said.
Following the decision, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police launched follow-up investigations, including taking action against several individuals linked to alleged misconduct, abuse of power and misappropriation identified in the report.
Zulkifli said the RCI had identified weaknesses in TH's governance, including the broad powers of the responsible minister, the appointment of board members without specific criteria and the influence of active politicians in the institution.
The RCI recommended comprehensive amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995, including clearer eligibility criteria and selection methods for board members based on relevant expertise.
It also recommended that active politicians not be appointed as TH chairman or board members.
Zulkifli said more than 75 per cent of the RCI's recommendations had been implemented by TH, while the remaining recommendations were being actively addressed.
He said reforms introduced since 2018 had helped strengthen TH's financial position, governance, investment quality and pilgrimage services.
He stressed that TH must never again become a victim of political interests or poor governance, adding that the trust placed in the institution by millions of depositors must be protected regardless of which government was in power.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate by MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Title: Zulkifli urges opposition MPs to return for Tabung Haji RCI debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has called for opposition members of Parliament to return to the Dewan Rakyat and debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji.
While briefing on the report, Zulkifli expressed disappointment over the decision by several opposition MPs to walk out of the Dewan Rakyat during the special sitting on the RCI.
He said the walkout was regrettable as the debate centred on an institution that held deep significance for Malaysia's Muslim community.
"I am deeply disappointed by the opposition's conduct this morning. We are discussing an institution that is dearly cherished by Muslims in Malaysia.
"Yet they chose to leave the House. Not all of them, but half of the opposition.
"I sincerely and wholeheartedly call on the opposition to remain in the House and debate this issue if they truly champion the agenda of Muslims in Malaysia," he said.
Earlier, opposition MPs staged a walkout from the Dewan Rakyat today after the Speaker rejected their call to postpone the special sitting
They had called for the sitting to be postponed until Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim returned to Parliament.
Zulkifli said Tabung Haji should never become a political battleground, describing it as an institution entrusted with safeguarding the savings and aspirations of millions of Muslim depositors.
"We may belong to different political parties and hold different views. We may debate vigorously in this House, but some institutions should never be dragged into the political arena. Tabung Haji is one of them.
"Tabung Haji does not belong to today's government, yesterday's government or any political party. It is the trust of Malaysia's Muslim community," he said.
He said every ringgit deposited with Tabung Haji represented years of sacrifice by ordinary Malaysians saving to perform the haj pilgrimage.
"They may not know what MFRS (Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards) is. They may not know what impairment is. They may never read financial statements. But they know one thing, they trust Tabung Haji.
"That trust was once betrayed by irresponsible parties, and today we are rebuilding it.
"Never again should political interests override the interests of depositors and the Muslim community," he said.

Title: Malaysia-Hong Kong dual IPO listing framework to take effect next month
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The simplified dual initial public offering (IPO) listing framework between Malaysia and Hong Kong will take effect next month, further strengthening capital market linkages between the two economies.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the framework was among the latest developments in Malaysia-Hong Kong economic ties, following a memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) and Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission on July 23.
"The MoU widens mutual recognition of funds to cover exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and real estate investment trusts (REITs), and opens a simplified dual IPO listing framework that will come into effect next month," he said.
He said this in his special remarks at the opening session of "Think Business, Think Hong Kong 2026" here today.
Loke said Bursa Malaysia had also been recognised as a Recognised Stock Exchange by Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Ltd (HKEX), enabling public limited companies listed on Bursa Malaysia to apply for a secondary listing in Hong Kong.
He said the development would provide Malaysian companies with greater access to Hong Kong's capital market and investors.
"Regulators can sign agreements and governments can open offices, but none of it counts until a Malaysian company actually files for that dual listing, or a Hong Kong fund manager actually brings a product to Malaysian investors," he said.
Loke also highlighted the growing connectivity between Malaysia and Hong Kong, noting that Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong are less than four hours apart by air and share the same time zone.
He said Cathay Pacific had added a fourth daily service on the Kuala Lumpur-Hong Kong route since March, reflecting growing commercial demand, while Malaysia Airlines added direct services from Kuala Lumpur to Shenzhen and Changsha in July, bringing its Greater China network to nine gateways.
On cargo connectivity, Loke said Hong Kong International Airport was among the world's busiest cargo gateways, while Port Klang sits along one of the world's most heavily used shipping lanes.
He said the combination of Hong Kong's strengths in logistics, trade finance, arbitration and professional services with Malaysia's growing exports of electronics, semiconductors and other high-value goods presented further opportunities for businesses in both markets.
Loke also urged businesses attending the symposium to leverage the opportunities created through the closer capital market linkages between Malaysia and Hong Kong.
He said the relationship between the two economies was considerably stronger than commonly perceived, with Hong Kong having been among Malaysia's significant investors for decades, while Malaysia is among Hong Kong's leading trading partners in ASEAN.
He added that closer cooperation in capital markets, trade and investment would continue to strengthen economic ties between Malaysia and Hong Kong.

Title: Body of missing 7-year-old found 3km downstream
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: The body of a seven-year-old Indonesian boy who fell into a river near a supermarket in Persiaran Subang Indah yesterday has been found.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the boy's body was found at 10.59am today, about three kilometres from where he was believed to have fallen into the river.
"The victim was found by personnel from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station and the department's Water Rescue Team (PPDA).
"The body was brought to the Fire and Rescue Department's control post at noon, where the victim's parents identified and confirmed his identity," he said.

Title: Turkiye MPs back historic law on reintegrating Kurdish militants
Article:
ISTANBUL: Turkish lawmakers on Monday voted through a bill offering limited amnesty for Kurdish PKK militants, a key step in the peace process that seeks to end decades of deadly violence.
The law is Turkiye's first legislative step towards ending the conflict and comes 18 months after Abdullah Ocalan, the jailed founder of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), urged his followers to disarm.
After 12 hours of debate, lawmakers voted by 468 in favour to 88 against, with six abstentions, for the so-called "terror-free Turkiye law" which envisages a return to civilian life for some of the PKK fighters who lay down their weapons without granting a total amnesty.
But crucially, the text does not specify what will become of Ocalan, 77, who has spent the past 27 years being held in solitary confinement on Imrali prison island near Istanbul.
Ocalan has played a key role in efforts to end the conflict, issuing a historic call in February 2025 for his fighters to disarm and embrace democratic means to defend the rights of Turkiye's Kurdish minority.
Backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) and the pro-Kurdish DEM party, the bill suspends prosecutions and prison sentences for some offences for between five and 10 years.
The move is expected to involve the release of around 3,500 PKK-linked detainees in an initial phase, lawmakers said – around a third of the number held in Turkish prisons.
If those covered by the measure do not reoffend during that period, investigations would be dropped and sentences considered served.
But those involved in serious crimes such as murder would be excluded – with the text making no mention of Ocalan.
Last week, Turkiye's vice president Cevdet Yilmaz told CNN Turk Ocalan's case "does not fall within the scope of this law" but said he would be "in a position to contribute to the peace process" without giving further details.
Following the vote, Yilmaz hailed the new law as a "historic step", saying "the 468 'yes' votes are of the utmost importance in terms of political consensus."
"We expect the disarmament and dissolution processes to be implemented as quickly as possible.. and subsequently for the relevant articles of the law to come into effect," he wrote on X.
Devlet Bahceli, a close Erdogan ally and head of the hardline nationalist MHP whose unexpected olive branch to Ocalan kickstarted the process in October 2024, also hailed the vote.
"May it bring good luck and success," he said, shaking hands with pro-Kurdish MPs from DEM – which also played a key role in the process, with its lawmakers regularly visiting Ocalan on Imrali island to pass messages back and forth.
With the vote, Turkey was "crossing a historic threshold", DEM MP Ceylan Akca told AFP.
"This is the first step of a long walk towards absolute and authentic equality. I choose to be optimistic," she said, admitting the vote had made her "more hopeful."
Ahead of the vote, the government had been keen to stress that the text was not a general amnesty law, aware of the misgivings of the Turkish public which has been scarred by decades of bloody conflict.
And the tension was evident as lawmakers held a heated debate in a session broadcast live on TRT public television.
"How can you negotiate with terrorists? ... You said they would be laying down their weapons unconditionally," said Turhan Comez, a lawmaker with the nationalist opposition Iyi party.
In May last year, the PKK announced it was disbanding following Ocalan's call and two months later, its militants took part in a historic disarmament ceremony in the mountains of northern Iraq where they began symbolically destroying their weapons.
But the PKK leadership has said excluding Ocalan from the legislation would be a red line, warning on Sunday that many of the bill's provisions would remain a "dead letter" if he were not freed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SD Guthrie Q2 earnings nearly double to RM987mil on industrial development, downstream gains
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: SD Guthrie Bhd's net profit nearly doubled to RM987 million in the second quarter ended June 30 from RM505 million a year earlier, driven by stronger contributions from its industrial development and downstream businesses.
Revenue, however, fell 4.4 per cent to RM4.94 billion from RM5.17 billion, the group said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
SD Guthrie said its industrial development segment recorded a pre-tax profit of RM529 million during the quarter, while its downstream business, SD Guthrie International, posted an eight per cent increase in pre-tax profit to RM136 million.
The stronger contributions helped offset a five per cent decline in pre-tax profit from the upstream segment, which was partly cushioned by higher realised crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel prices of RM4,283 and RM3,436 per tonne, respectively.
For the first half of financial year 2026 (FY26), net profit rose 44 per cent to RM1.55 billion from RM1.07 billion a year earlier, despite revenue declining four per cent to RM9.63 billion from RM9.99 billion.
SD Guthrie chairman Tan Sri Nik Norzrul Thani Nik Hassan Thani said the group's strategic and disciplined execution had delivered encouraging results despite economic and geopolitical uncertainties.
President and group chief executive officer Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad said the first-half performance reflected progress in transforming the group into a more diversified organisation beyond its traditional plantation base.
He said the group would continue expanding its industrial development and renewable energy businesses through strategic partnerships, while strengthening earnings resilience and developing new growth engines.
For FY26, SD Guthrie expects tightening global supply and resilient demand to support CPO prices.
It said potential El Nino conditions towards year-end, Indonesia's B50 biodiesel mandate and firm crude oil prices amid geopolitical tensions could further influence the market.
The upstream segment will focus on operational efficiency and climate risk management, while the downstream business will continue diversifying its customer base and markets and pursuing cost optimisation.
The industrial development segment is expected to make a stronger contribution to earnings, while the renewable energy business will continue laying the foundation for longer-term growth.
"Overall, the group remains positive on its FY26 outlook, supported by favourable market dynamics, operational resilience and strong execution momentum in its industrial development segment.
"At the same time, the group will continue to navigate market and weather-related uncertainties while maintaining disciplined execution across its businesses," SD Guthrie said.

Title: Several detained as police, MACC probe TH RCI findings - Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) have launched investigations into findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with several individuals detained over alleged misconduct.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan told the Dewan Rakyat that enforcement action began after the Cabinet decided on July 29 to make the RCI report public and order full investigations into its findings.
"The MACC and the police have acted swiftly by commencing follow-up investigations and detaining several key individuals linked to elements of misconduct in this RCI report," he said during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the report.
Zulkifli said the action demonstrated the government's commitment to ensuring that no party was protected if found to have abused power or breached the trust involving TH funds.
He said TH had also provided full cooperation to enforcement agencies, submitting six reports to police and another six to MACC for further action.
The RCI identified 14 problematic investments associated with losses running into billions of ringgit, including Putrajaya Perdana, Al-Rawda, BTH Indo Plantations, Trurich and Felda Global Ventures (FGV).
Zulkifli said the investments were among matters being examined following the RCI's findings.
He said TH had appointed Ernst & Young (EY) and law firms Skrine & Co, Zain & Co and Tajuddin & Co to conduct gap analyses and recommend improvements relating to the 14 investments.
The findings were presented to the TH board and the recommended improvements have since been implemented, he said.
The findings were presented to the TH board and the recommended improvements had since been implemented, he said.
Among the investments highlighted by the RCI was TH's RM1.55 billion upfront payment to Al-Rawda between 2015 and 2017 to lease four hotels in Makkah and Madinah.
Zulkifli said Al-Rawda subsequently failed to make rental payments, prompting TH to initiate enforcement proceedings in Saudi Arabia.
An arbitration award in April 2023 ordered Al-Rawda to pay TH Saudi Riyal 859 million.
However, the company was found to lack the financial capacity to settle the amount.
Zulkifli said a settlement agreement reached in November 2024 resulted in Al-Rawda paying only Saudi Riyal 14.9 million before failing to comply with the agreement.
TH subsequently terminated the settlement and resumed efforts to recover the outstanding arbitration award, including by appointing an asset-tracing specialist.
Zulkifli said the RCI findings had also prompted wider reforms to TH's governance, financial reporting and investment management.
"The action demonstrates the government's continued commitment and that there will be no compromise for any party involved in abuse of power or breach of trust involving the sacred funds of the country's pilgrims," he said.
On Saturday, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, decreed that investigations into the RCI report on TH should be conducted exhaustively.
His Majesty said this was important to ensure that every party responsible was subjected to appropriate action and to prevent similar issues from recurring.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate by MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Title: Schools closed as Indonesia battles wildfires
Article:
SURABAYA: Dozens of Indonesian schools were shuttered for a second day Tuesday against the spreading haze of wildfires plaguing the archipelago at the start of a long and intense dry season worsened by El Nino.
In West Kalimantan on the island of Borneo that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei, the mayor of Pontianak ordered schools closed due to the smoke wafting over the city from fires elsewhere.
Public records show Pontianak has tens of thousands of public school pupils.
Children will learn from home for as long as air quality remains poor, mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono said in a statement Monday, without stating how many schools were affected.
"We have started to feel it, especially at night and in the morning, as haze has already blanketed the city of Pontianak," he said.
On the island of Java, firefighters battled flames for a ninth day at a national park that has lost 900 hectares to an inferno that broke out on Monday last week.
The blaze at the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, a major tourist attraction closed to visitors since Saturday, is one of several wildfires that have drawn in nearly 50,000 firefighters countrywide.
Indonesia is forecast to experience an unusually tough dry season this year with high risk for drought and wildfires due in part to the El Nino weather phenomenon, the BMKG weather agency has said.
More than 107,000 hectares of land have burnt countrywide so far this year.
Authorities insist that food stocks remain adequate.
The fire at the Bromo park in East Java has consumed nearly 900 hectares, or more than 2,200 acres, by Tuesday morning.
This is equivalent to over 1,200 football fields and nearly two percent of the total park area.
"We're making our best effort and mobilising everything... to extinguish and wet-down the area," local disaster official Satriyo Nurseno told AFP.
"We hope that today we can put out the fire in all areas, then carry out soaking so that the fire does not reignite."
Three water-bombing helicopters and fire trucks were providing support to about 200 firefighters, forest rangers, police and soldiers helping to put out the blaze.
According to the BNPB disaster agency, more than 48,000 personnel have been deployed to fight fires in six provinces.
And Security Minister Djamari Chaniago said Monday Indonesia has deployed 43 helicopters and up to 15 fixed-wing planes for cloud seeding where needed.
The process involves spraying particles such as silver iodide and salt from aircraft to produce rainfall, but depends on clouds being present.
As Indonesia braces for the worst effects of El Nino, the BMKG said the average air temperature in July was 27C – higher than the 26.2C average.
It was the highest such jump for July since 1991.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns.
In India and Southeast Asia, it typically causes drier conditions.
The last El Nino helped make 2023 and 2024 the two hottest years globally on record.
The land lost to wildfires in Indonesia so far this year is double the area burnt in 2023.

Title: Reforms help TH achieve record RM4.64bil investment income in 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) recorded its highest-ever investment income of RM4.64 billion last year following reforms to its investment strategy, governance and financial management, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the performance reflected the results of reforms implemented since 2018 to strengthen TH's financial position and improve the quality of its investments.
"Tabung Haji has successfully recorded the highest investment income in its history, amounting to RM4.64 billion in 2025, as a result of improved investment quality as well as stronger governance and transparency in the management of the institution," he said.
Zulkifli said the institution had also gradually increased its profit distribution rate from 1.25 per cent in 2018 to 3.5 per cent for 2025.
"The 2025 rate was the highest in eight years."
He said the improvement had been achieved despite TH continuing to deal with RM2.6 billion in legacy assets that had required impairment after 2018.
Zulkifli said the restructuring of TH's assets and liabilities had helped restore its financial position, clean up its balance sheet and rebuild its financial reserves.
The reforms were implemented following the institution's financial crisis, which saw its asset-liability deficit exceed RM10 billion in the fourth quarter of 2018.
The government subsequently undertook a restructuring plan involving the transfer of less competitive and problematic assets to government-owned Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB).
Zulkifli said the recovery had enabled TH to focus on delivering sustainable returns to depositors while maintaining its ability to support the cost of performing the haj.
He said TH had maintained the haj cost at RM33,300 for three consecutive seasons from 2024 to 2026 despite rising inflation and increased operating costs.
The institution had also improved the quality of its investment portfolio and strengthened governance as part of a wider nine-point transformation agenda.
"The agenda included restoring financial strength, strengthening governance and accountability, improving investment quality, providing sustainable returns to depositors, protecting depositors' interests and developing a stronger and more resilient Islamic institution."
Zulkifli said TH's improved performance was also reflected in its international recognition for haj management.
He said TH had received the Labbaik Diamond Award for two consecutive years and had secured the award five times in succession.
"Under the leadership of a professional, competent and credible board and management team, Tabung Haji has returned to a stronger and more sustainable path through a strategic reform plan and better governance."
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate from MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Title: 52,750 Rumah Selangorku units completed as of mid-2026
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A total of 52,750 Rumah Selangorku (RSKU) units involving 167 projects had been completed and handed over to buyers as of mid-2026, the Selangor State Legislative Assembly was told today.
State Housing and Culture Committee chairman Datuk Borhan Aman Shah said another 34,287 RSKU units involving 68 projects were under construction during the same period.
He said the achievement showed that the implementation of affordable housing provision in the state was on a positive trajectory towards achieving the target set by the state government.
"To ensure that more affordable homes priced below RM250,000 can be provided, the state government has implemented the RSKU 3.0 Policy, which sets the composition of RSKU provision according to development zones and areas.
"In addition, the state government has also introduced several incentives for developers, including a 100 per cent exemption from development charges, as well as the implementation of the RSKU Harapan Policy and Rumah Idaman MBI Selangor to encourage the provision of more affordable homes," he said.
He was responding to a question from Yew Jia Haur (PH-Teratai) on the latest status of the construction and handover of RSKU units as of mid-2026.
Meanwhile, Borhan said that for projects experiencing delays or categorised as sick projects, the state government, through the Selangor Housing and Property Board (LPHS), had implemented intervention measures covering monitoring, enforcement and administrative aspects to ensure that the projects could be revived and completed according to plan.
He said the state government would not compromise with developers who failed to comply with the project implementation schedule, including the issuance of compliance notices, implementation of a recovery plan and issuance of stop-work orders.
"In addition, restrictions on the consideration of new development applications, as well as additional conditions for project approvals, will also be imposed," he said.

Title: Death toll in Gaza exceeds 75,000, says Palestinian ambassador
Article:
MOSCOW: The death toll in the Gaza Strip has exceeded 75,000 since the escalation began in 2023, Palestinian Ambassador to Russia Abdel Hafiz Nofal said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
"According to available data, the total number of dead in the Gaza Strip has exceeded 75,000, and the number of injured has exceeded 250,000," the ambassador told Russian newspaper
Izvestia
.
The diplomat also noted that many of the dead remain buried under rubble.
On Oct 9, 2025, Israel and Hamas, with the mediation of Egypt, Qatar, the United States (US) and Turkiye, agreed to implement the first phase of the peace plan presented by US President Donald Trump.
The following day, a ceasefire went into effect in Gaza.
In accordance with the agreement, Israeli troops withdrew to the so-called Yellow Line, retaining control of over 50 per cent of the strip's territory.
However, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected the US-led Gaza plan endorsed by Hamas, putting distance between himself and President Donald Trump as he tries to shore up his base ahead of close elections.
After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism of the plan, and despite receiving assurances that Israel would not need to start withdrawing in Gaza immediately, Netanyahu explicitly opposed the deal following pushback from his right-wing allies.
"Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu said, referring to the plan Hamas agreed to in late July.
The Israeli military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed, and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens", he told a cabinet meeting.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gamuda climbs ESG rankings
Article:
KUALALUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd has been recognised for its sustainability efforts after being included in TIME and Statista's World's Most Sustainable Companies 2026 list while also advancing to the highest four-star grading band under the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia index.
It was the only Malaysian company recognised in the Resource Generation & Infrastructure category, which covers businesses involved in utilities, heavy engineering, mining support and raw material supply.
It ranked 239th globally among 750 companies selected from more than 5,800 firms across 43 countries.
Gamuda said its inclusion in the global list reflects the strength of its sustainability practices and disclosures, while reinforcing its position as a trusted partner in delivering infrastructure and development projects that support long-term economic and community outcomes.
The company also recorded an improvement in its Bursa Malaysia FTSE4Good ESG rating to 3.7, lifting it into the highest four-star ESG grading band under the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index.
Gamuda said the rating upgrade was primarily driven by stronger performance in the social and governance pillars, further strengthening its ESG risk management capabilities.
The improved rating is expected to enhance the group's appeal to institutional investors, support inclusion in ESG-focused investment mandates and improve access to sustainability-linked financing.
It could also strengthen Gamuda's position in bidding for projects where ESG credentials are increasingly becoming an important pre-qualification requirement.
The company said the latest recognitions underscore its view that sustainability is a core part of its business strategy and long-term value creation approach.
As it continues to expand across its key regional markets, Gamuda said it remains committed to delivering resilient, responsibly governed projects that benefit communities and support sustainable development, guided by its Gamuda Green Plan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rehda hails 10-year housing roadmap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Real Estate and Housing Developers' Association Malaysia (Rehda) has welcomed the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, describing it as a comprehensive framework that will help shape the future of Malaysia's housing sector.
Rehda said the policy's theme, "Humanising Housing", aligns with its long-held view that housing goes beyond the construction of physical structures and should focus on delivering quality, affordable, liveable and sustainable homes for Malaysians.
Rehda Malaysia president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said the association was particularly encouraged by the policy's emphasis on data-driven housing planning, including the use of big data analytics and housing projections based on locality, existing supply, vacancy rates, housing types, income levels and price categories.
The association also welcomed the policy's focus on expanding pathways to homeownership through initiatives such as Rent-to-Own schemes, the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme, Shared Ownership programmes and long-term fixed-rate mortgages.
Zaini said access to financing remains a major challenge for many prospective homebuyers.
"We welcome more flexible and inclusive financing solutions, particularly for middle-income households that may not qualify for affordable housing programmes but continue to face affordability constraints in the open market," he said.
Rehda further expressed support for measures aimed at creating more liveable communities, improving integration between housing and transportation, promoting urban renewal and enhancing housing standards.
The association highlighted the proposed integration of housing and transportation policies as a timely initiative that would improve connectivity between homes, employment centres, public transport and essential amenities.
However, Rehda cautioned that certain proposals under the policy would require careful study and extensive engagement with industry stakeholders, particularly the proposed transition from the current Sell-Then-Build (STB) model to a Build-Then-Sell (BTS) system between 2027 and 2035.
While acknowledging the government's intention to strengthen homebuyer protection, Zaini said any fundamental change to the housing delivery model must take into account its impact on financing, cash flow, holding costs, housing prices and overall supply.
Rehda noted that the STB model has successfully facilitated the delivery of more than 6.5 million housing units nationwide over the years and believes it should continue to coexist alongside BTS if the latter is introduced.
Overall, Rehda described the National Housing Policy as a positive and comprehensive framework for strengthening Malaysia's housing ecosystem and reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with the government to ensure its successful implementation.
The association also pledged to continue encouraging its members to uphold their nation-building role by delivering quality and affordable homes in a timely and sustainable manner.

Title: Tabung Haji must never again be victim of political interests - Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) must never again become a victim of political interests, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said today.
Zulkifli said the institution belonged to Malaysian Muslim depositors and should not be dragged into political battles, regardless of which government was in power.
"TH is not owned by today's government, yesterday's government or any political party. TH is the trust of Malaysian Muslims," he said during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into TH.
He said lawmakers should draw lessons from the RCI findings, which identified political influence, weak governance and the appointment of active politicians to key positions as factors that contributed to the institution's problems.
The RCI found that
political considerations
had influenced several key decisions involving TH between 2014 and 2020.
It also found that weaknesses in the Tabung Haji Act 1995 gave the minister responsible for TH wide discretion over matters including haj operations, fund management and investment decisions.
According to the report, the Act did not set specific qualification requirements for appointments to the TH board beyond requiring members to be Malaysian citizens and Muslims.
The RCI said this had resulted in several political figures being appointed to the board between 2014 and 2018, contributing to perceptions of political interference.
Zulkifli said the RCI had recommended that active politicians not be appointed as chairman or members of the TH board.
He said the recommendation was being addressed through a new approach to leadership appointments based on integrity, competence, experience and fit-and-proper criteria.
"We can differ in political parties, we can have different views and debate strongly in this House, but there are institutions that should not be dragged into the political arena.
"TH is one of them," he said.
Zulkifli said every ringgit deposited with TH represented the savings and aspirations of Malaysians preparing for the pilgrimage, including parents saving for their children, retirees, fishermen, farmers and small traders.
"They may not know what MFRS or impairment means. They may not read financial statements, but they know one thing — they trust TH," he said.
He said that trust had previously been undermined by governance failures, adding that the government was rebuilding confidence through institutional reforms.
Zulkifli said TH had implemented more than 75 per cent of the relevant RCI recommendations and was continuing to address the remaining recommendations.
He said the government would strengthen the Tabung Haji Act, board governance and institutional oversight to prevent a recurrence of the problems identified by the RCI.
"We must never again allow TH to become a victim of the greed for power.
"We must never again allow political interests to take precedence over the interests of depositors and Muslims," he said.
Zulkifli also stressed that TH's financial figures must not be manipulated to conceal weaknesses or misconduct.
He said all decisions affecting the institution must ultimately be guided by what was best for its depositors and the Malaysian Muslim community.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate by MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.

Title: 61 groups object to genetically modified rice field trial in Perak
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Sixty-one organisations have objected to a proposed confined field trial involving genetically modified MR219 rice in Kampung Kepayang, Perak.
The coalition, comprising farmers, consumer, and environmental groups, said it submitted a formal objection to the Department of Biosafety's director-general via the Unified Public Consultation (UPC) website on Aug 7.
It said the application by Zen Cropscience Sdn Bhd was identical to a proposal for a similar MR219 trial in Tambun Tulang, Perlis, in 2019, reiterating its previous concerns.
According to the coalition, MR219 has been genetically modified to tolerate glyphosate and resist diseases caused by bacteria and fungi.
It said the proposed trial raised concerns over potential genetic contamination of conventional and wild rice, while claiming Malaysia's Biosafety Act 2007 did not provide adequate statutory protection, legal liability or redress for farmers who might suffer economic losses from GM contamination.
"The financial burden would fall entirely upon the affected farmers," it said in a statement today.
The coalition also claimed that glyphosate-tolerant MR219 could encourage greater use of the herbicide, while expressing concern over potential residues entering the food supply.
It said a fact sheet by the Department of Biosafety acknowledged that acute toxicological data for the GM rice was still unavailable.
The group said Pertubuhan Persaudaraan Pesawah Malaysia (PeSAWAH) had opposed GM MR219 since 2019, adding that farmers had experienced problems with herbicide-resistant rice varieties such as Clearfield.
It claimed weeds had developed resistance to the herbicide, resulting in increased pesticide use, higher production costs and soil degradation.
The coalition further raised concerns about glyphosate's alleged impact on soil microorganisms and paddy ecosystem biodiversity, as well as potential effects on organic production and export markets.
It cited China in 2008 as an example, claiming rice exports had faced rejection from European markets following contamination concerns.
The organisations said alternative weed and disease management approaches, including the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), were available without relying on genetic modification.
"Although the application concerns a confined field trial, the research should be cancelled, simply because genetically modified organisms could not be completely contained once released into the environment," the coalition added.
It said modified genes could potentially spread through cross-pollination and germination, while GM and non-GM crops could also become mixed during harvesting, storage or transportation.
The coalition said the proposed trial was inappropriate amid what it described as growing consumer interest in organic food.
It said the 61 organisations had united in opposing the field trial because of what they regarded as potential socioeconomic, environmental and health risks.
The statement was issued on behalf of the 61 organisations, with PeSAWAH's Abdul Rashid Yob, Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) representative Mageswari Sangaralingam and Malaysia Food Sovereignty Forum (FKMM) representative Nurfitri Amir Muhammad named as spokespeople.

Title: High dividend pressure drove TH into risky investments, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pressure to maintain high annual dividend payouts drove Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to make high-risk investments that eventually resulted in losses amounting to billions of ringgit, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) identified 14 problematic investments linked to losses running into billions of ringgit, including Putrajaya Perdana, Al-Rawda, PT TH Indo Plantation, True Rich and FGV.
He said the investments were approved between 2010 and 2017 following recommendations by TH's board.
Citing the Al-Rawda deal as an example, Zulkifli said TH paid about RM1.55 billion upfront between 2015 and 2017 to lease four hotels in Makkah and Madinah for periods ranging from 10 to 18 years.
"This was an extraordinary transaction. It was not normal. As if that was not enough, TH also appointed Al-Rawda to operate all four hotels under a management agreement, while receiving only a promissory note personally guaranteed by the company's owner.
"Pressure to announce high dividends year after year drove TH to undertake several high-risk investments, resulting in investment losses amounting to billions of ringgit," he said during the special Dewan Rakyat sitting on the RCI report into TH.
He said the dispute was eventually decided in TH's favour in April 2023, with Al-Rawda ordered to pay SAR899 million.
However, the company was found to be financially incapable of settling the amount, prompting TH to continue enforcement efforts, including appointing asset-tracing specialists.
Zulkifli said TH also incurred losses of more than RM1 billion from its investment in FGV after continuing to hold the shares despite their value plunging by more than 80 per cent.
"When the share price collapsed, TH continued holding the shares despite their value falling by more than 80 per cent, while only changing its impairment policy to hide and obscure the losses," he said.
He also highlighted TH's investment in Putrajaya Perdana, saying its then chairman simultaneously served as chairman of the company.
"The same person chaired both TH and Putrajaya Perdana. The company was then involved in 1MDB transactions. In the end, TH suffered losses of RM145.3 million," he said.
Zulkifli also questioned TH's purchase of land at Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) from 1MDB at the height of the state investment fund's controversy.
"Was the investment made in TH's interest or to solve other parties' problems?" he said.

Title: DBKL cuts red tape for restaurants, food operators
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) is moving to ease business operations for restaurant and food premises operators by introducing three major improvements aimed at streamlining services and cutting red tape across the federal capital.
The enhancements are establishing a RM30 monthly permit for five-foot way outdoor seating, simplifying minor renovation permits through branch offices, and offering a faster 24-hour reopening route for premises closed due to hygiene breaches once safety conditions are met.
DBKL said the measures follow recent engagement sessions involving Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud, the Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Chinese Coffee Shop and Tea Shop Owners' Association, and the Malaysia Muslim Restaurant Operators Association (Presma).
"These improvements will apply to all traders who meet the stipulated requirements, regardless of their background or type of premises," DBKL said in a statement today.
Under the new outdoor seating guidelines, operators can apply through DBKL branch offices based on their parliamentary constituency.
The permit costs RM30 a month for each set of tables and chairs, subject to location suitability, five-foot-way width and unobstructed access for pedestrians, wheelchair users and emergency services.
For minor non-structural works, such as replacing tiles or ceilings, operators will only need to complete a form and notify DBKL. Permits can be issued directly by the relevant branch office.
For premises ordered to close over hygiene breaches, DBKL said reopening could be considered as early as 24 hours after thorough cleaning, subject to a mandatory inspection and confirmation of full compliance.
DBKL said standardising procedures across its branch offices would reduce differing interpretations by enforcement officers and provide greater certainty for business operators.
It said the measures were part of efforts to streamline services, reduce unnecessary procedures and create a more conducive business environment without compromising safety, hygiene, accessibility and the public interest.

Title: PwC review found TH in critical financial position, Dewan told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government in 2018 appointed one of the Big Four accounting firms to reassess Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) financial position and performance after concerns were raised over its accounts.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the new TH board appointed PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) to review the institution's financial position in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
He said the move followed concerns raised by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Auditor General over the gap between TH's assets and liabilities, as well as its accounting practices at the time.
"The new Tabung Haji board in 2018 appointed a Big Four audit firm, PwC, to reassess Tabung Haji's financial position and performance according to proper and recognised accounting standards," he said when presenting the government's explanation of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH in the Dewan Rakyat.
Zulkifli said PwC's assessment found TH in a critical financial position, with the deficit between its assets and liabilities exceeding RM10 billion in the fourth quarter of 2018.
He said the situation put TH at risk of being unable to declare a profit distribution and facing large-scale panic withdrawals by depositors.
The findings eventually led to a restructuring and recovery plan to restore TH's solvency and ensure its long-term sustainability.
Zulkifli said the RCI also found that TH's financial reporting at the time did not accurately reflect its actual financial position.
Had Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) been fully applied, TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017 instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, he said.
"The changes to the impairment policy twice in the same year resulted in financial reporting that did not reflect Tabung Haji's actual position."
He said TH's financial statements had been prepared fully in accordance with applicable accounting standards since 2018, while profit distributions since 2022 had been based on audited annual financial statements.
The government is also reviewing amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to strengthen provisions on accounting standards and introduce penalties for misreporting financial statements.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate from MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.
On Saturday, the His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia decreed that the investigation into the RCI Report on TH should be carried out exhaustively.
His Majesty said that this step is important to ensure that every responsible party is subjected to appropriate action, in addition to ensuring that the same issue does not recur in the future.
Enforcement agencies have also stepped up action following the release of the RCI report on TH, with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has since detained several people as part of its probe.

Title: Govt denies TH assets sold to non-Muslims, Chinese interests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has denied claims that assets belonging to Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) were sold to non-Muslims or Chinese interests as part of its restructuring exercise.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the assets transferred under the 2018 recovery plan were sold to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), a special-purpose vehicle wholly owned by the government.
"No assets were sold to non-Muslims or to China, as alleged by certain irresponsible parties," he said when presenting the government's explanation of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH in the Dewan Rakyat.
Zulkifli said TH had transferred underperforming and problematic assets worth RM9.7 billion to UJSB at a value of RM19.9 billion as part of a plan to close the institution's asset-liability gap, which stood at about RM10 billion at the time.
The transaction involved 100 listed shares, 29 properties and a palm oil plantation company.
He said UJSB financed the acquisition through sukuk that were fully subscribed by TH.
As part of the arrangement, TH was also granted a Right of First Refusal (ROFR), giving it priority to purchase the assets if UJSB decided to sell them in the future.
"This means the assets can return to Tabung Haji if Tabung Haji wishes to acquire them."
However, Zulkifli stressed that the ROFR did not oblige TH to buy back the assets.
"Any repurchase would be subject to commercial valuation and the assets' suitability under TH's investment criteria."
He said the transfer was carried out to rescue and restore TH's financial position following the institution's financial crisis.
"The plan was not created because the government wanted to take Tabung Haji's assets."
Zulkifli said TH had since exercised the arrangement to reacquire some of the assets after its financial position improved.
Among them was a plot of land at the Tun Razak Exchange (TRX), which was sold for RM400 million in 2018 and subsequently bought back by TH for RM270 million based on its current market value.
TH also reacquired UJ Estates Holdings Sdn Bhd's palm oil plantation assets, which had previously been sold for RM800 million, for RM695 million based on market value, including RM115 million in cash.
Zulkifli said the transactions demonstrated that assets transferred under the restructuring exercise could be reassessed and reacquired where commercially viable and in the best interests of TH's depositors.
He stressed that decisions involving TH's assets must be guided by the interests of its depositors rather than political considerations.
"Tabung Haji does not belong to today's government, yesterday's government or any political party. It is a trust belonging to Malaysia's Muslims."
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate from MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Title: Typhoon Dolphin's vast storm system pushes inland, threatens central China
Article:
XIANGYANG: Typhoon Dolphin churned deeper inland to the central Chinese province of Hubei on Tuesday, prompting the closure of tourist areas and suspension of construction projects, as forecasters warned of the danger of extreme rainfall in the province's mountainous northwest.
The strongest typhoon to hit China this year, Dolphin packed an unusually resilient storm system that travelled nearly 6,000 km before making landfall over the weekend, drenching the country's eastern coast and bringing with it a sprawling cloud field.
Hubei, a major auto and high-tech electronics manufacturing hub and home to more than 58 million people, was struck by two rare tornadoes last month in the wake of Typhoon Maysak, which killed at least 11 people.
On Tuesday, the National Meteorological Center renewed an orange alert for heavy rain, the second-highest warning level, with northwestern  Hubei expected to receive as much as 250 mm of rain in a 24-hour period.
Hubei authorities have issued a yellow warning for cities including Xiangyang, Huanggang and Suizhou, citing a heightened risk of flooding and landslides.
Scenic areas across the province have announced temporary closures, including the popular Three Gorges Dam tourist area in Yichang.
Of 107 major highway and waterway construction projects underway in the province, 26 projects deemed high-risk have been suspended.
Dolphin's peripheral airflow will be forced to rise when it encounters the mountains in Hubei's western region, causing rainfall to intensify several times over, Wang Xiaoling, deputy director of Hubei's provincial meteorological observatory, told local newspaper Hubei Daily.
In neighbouring Henan province, authorities issued a red flash-flood alert as the storm continues to channel moisture northward. The storm's reach will be felt as far as Beijing, more than 1,000 km to the north of Hubei.
Four districts on the capital's outskirts activated Level I emergency flood responses, as the city braced for the expected onset of more than one-third of its annual rainfall over 24 hours starting late on Tuesday.
Japan is also preparing for landslides, flooding and strong winds after the Japan Meteorological Agency said Typhoon No. 15, Chan-hom, could move across Japan's mainland later on Tuesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RCI: TH crisis stems from years of weak governance, political  interference
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The financial crisis at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) was  the result of years of weak governance, political interference, risky  investment decisions and failures to accurately reflect the institution's  financial position, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr  Zulkifli Hasan said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) found that the  problems had accumulated over more than a decade, with weaknesses in  governance, particularly in the appointment of its leadership, among the key  contributing factors.
"The crisis at Tabung Haji did not happen overnight. It was  the accumulated result of greed and misconduct, weak governance, interference  by certain interests, risky investment decisions and failure to transparently  reflect its financial position," he said when explaining the government's  position on the RCI report.
He said the RCI had identified weaknesses in the powers of the  minister in charge, the appointment of board members without specific criteria  and political influence within the institution.
Among its recommendations was a comprehensive review of the Tabung  Haji Act 1995, including clearer eligibility criteria and selection methods for  board members based on relevant expertise.
The RCI also recommended that active politicians should not be  appointed chairman or members of the TH board.
Zulkifli said the government had acted on the recommendation by  ensuring TH's leadership, including its board and management, was appointed  based on integrity, competence, ability and experience, using fit-and-proper  criteria aligned with the framework adopted by Bank Negara Malaysia.
He said reforms had also been introduced to strengthen TH's  financial reporting and governance.
"Since 2018, TH's financial statements have been prepared  fully in accordance with applicable accounting standards, while profit  distributions since 2022 have been based on audited annual financial  statements."
Zulkifli said the government was reviewing amendments to the TH  Act to strengthen provisions on accounting standards and penalties for  misreporting financial statements.
A task force comprising the TH chairman, Bank Negara governor and  Securities Commission chairman had also been established to examine the  regulatory framework for TH's fund management and investments.
"The task force has agreed to recommend that the management  of funds and investments by Tabung Haji be regulated by the Securities  Commission, while pilgrimage management remains under the minister responsible  for religious affairs.
"Tabung Haji will remain as one unified entity."
Zulkifli said the RCI had made 25 recommendations under five main  areas, with TH having implemented more than 75 per cent of the recommendations.
He said the remaining recommendations were being implemented.
The RCI also identified 14 problematic investments associated with  losses running into billions of ringgit, including Putrajaya Perdana, Al-Rawda,  BTH Indo Plantations, Trurich and Felda Global Ventures (FGV).
Zulkifli said several of the investments had been approved by the  minister following recommendations by the board between 2010 and 2017.
He said the findings underscored the need to ensure that TH  remained focused on protecting the interests of its depositors.
"Tabung Haji is not owned by today's government, yesterday's  government or any political party. It is the trust of Malaysian Muslims,"  he said.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to  discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's  explanation, followed by questions and debate from MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's  management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including  political interference in management and the distribution of profits without  adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of  investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4  billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian  Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Article:

Title: [UPDATED] Zaliha slams PN MPs over walkout during Tabung Haji RCI debate
Article:

Title: AI helps Asian airports squeeze more from existing capacity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) could help Asian airports handle rising passenger traffic by improving the use of existing runways, gates and terminals, reducing the need to wait years for costly infrastructure expansion, said Assaia chief executive officer Christiaan Hen.
AI can identify bottlenecks during aircraft turnarounds in real time, allowing airport and airline teams to intervene before disruptions on the ground develop into flight delays, he said.
AI offers a different approach by helping airports increase the capacity of existing infrastructure through efficient day-to-day operations and optimised resource allocation, he said.
The technology is becoming increasingly relevant as passenger traffic across Asia grows, while airports face labour shortages, rising operational complexity and the high cost and long lead times associated with physical expansion.
Hen said many flight delays begin on the ground rather than in the air, with aircraft turnarounds involving a tightly coordinated sequence of baggage handling, passenger disembarking, refuelling, cleaning, catering and boarding.
"The turnaround is a highly interconnected operation, so even a small delay in baggage handling, disembarking, refuelling, cleaning or boarding can quickly cascade through the rest of the process," he said.
Assaia's annual Turnaround Report, which analyses more than 450,000 aircraft turnarounds at airports globally, found that flights delayed by at least 15 minutes took longer to complete baggage offloading than flights that departed on time.
It also found that departure delays of more than six minutes are typically unrecoverable, increasing the risk of knock-on disruptions across an airline's daily schedule.
Assaia's ApronAI platform uses computer vision and AI to monitor aircraft turnaround activities and automatically timestamp key milestones, including disembarking, baggage loading and unloading, refuelling, catering, cleaning, boarding and pushback.
The system compares the progress of each activity against the planned turnaround timeline and alerts operations teams when a task begins to fall behind schedule.
"For example, if baggage unloading takes longer than expected or refuelling starts late, airport and airline operations teams can intervene immediately before the delay cascades into other turnaround activities and ultimately affects the aircraft's departure time," Hen said.
The technology can also identify recurring bottlenecks at specific aircraft stands, during particular processes or at certain times of day, allowing airports to address systemic problems rather than simply responding to individual delays.
Japan's New Chitose Airport in Hokkaido, the first airport in the Asia-Pacific region to adopt Assaia's technology, illustrates the growing use of AI by airports seeking to maintain operational reliability as passenger demand increases, Hen said.
Japan has built a reputation for operational efficiency, while New Chitose serves as Hokkaido's main international gateway and is central to Hokkaido Airports' plans to expand international connectivity, particularly with Southeast Asia.
For passengers, greater use of AI could mean fewer unexpected delays, more reliable departure times and smoother journeys, including shorter waits for aircraft gates and baggage delivery.
"Passengers rarely think about what happens while an aircraft is on stand, but those activities have a direct impact on their journey.
"For passengers, including those travelling to and from Malaysia, this means fewer unexpected delays, greater confidence that flights will depart on time and a smoother experience on arrival, with less waiting for a jet bridge or baggage delivery," he said.
Assaia's technology integrates with existing airport and airline operational systems, including airport operational databases and systems supporting airport collaborative decision-making processes.
It also uses existing airside cameras to provide a real-time view of aircraft turnaround operations.
The system combines visual and operational data to identify and timestamp turnaround milestones, monitor activities and flag operational risks, giving airports, airlines and ground handlers a shared view of each aircraft's progress.
Hen said integrating AI into the complex airport ecosystem was a bigger challenge than the technology itself.
"An airport is an ecosystem of airlines, airports, ground handlers and service providers, each with their own systems and priorities and streams of data. For AI to deliver value, it needs to provide a shared, trusted operational picture that helps everyone make faster, better-informed decisions," he said.
"Cost is also naturally an important consideration, but AI is increasingly becoming a longer-term operational investment. And ultimately, adoption depends on demonstrating measurable improvements, whether that's reducing delays, increasing aircraft utilisation or protecting margins.
"As more airports report tangible operational and financial benefits, confidence in AI adoption will continue to grow," he said.
Potential gains can be significant, says Hen.
At JFK Terminal 4 in New York, Assaia said its technology reduced average ground delays by about five minutes per flight, representing potential annual cost savings of US$40 million.
Alaska Airlines reported a 17 per cent increase in on-time departures, while Berlin Brandenburg Airport achieved a 69 per cent reduction in ground delays, according to the company.
"These improvements translate into more reliable journeys for passengers and more consistent operations for airports," Hen said.
He said AI could also help airports increase flight capacity without immediately undertaking major physical expansion by improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure.
Hen said airports had two forms of capacity: physical capacity, determined by terminals, gates and runways, and operational capacity, determined by how efficiently those assets are used.
"Airports are beginning to recognise there is significant untapped capacity within existing operations. By reducing unnecessary delays and enabling gates to be used more efficiently, AI helps airports accommodate more flights without immediately building additional infrastructure," he said.
Assaia's ResourceManager has demonstrated the potential to increase stand capacity by up to 16 additional flights a day, he said.
For many airports operating close to capacity, AI-powered technology is one of the fastest and most cost-effective ways to support future growth," Hen said.
The technology could also become an increasingly important competitive tool as Asian airports vie to strengthen their positions as regional aviation hubs.
While geography and physical infrastructure remain important factors in determining hub locations, operational performance is becoming a bigger differentiator, Hen said.
Airlines need predictable operations because delays can affect aircraft utilisation across their wider networks, while passengers increasingly expect reliable and seamless journeys.
"The airports that combine modern infrastructure with intelligent, data-driven operations will be best placed to compete for airlines, passengers and future investment. In this sense, AI is becoming part of an airport's competitive strategy," he said.

Title: Zulkifli: Five Bank Negara warnings over Tabung Haji's finances went unheeded
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) issued five warnings to Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2014 over the institution's widening asset-liability gap and the risks associated with paying high profit distributions, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the warnings came as TH's financial position deteriorated, with its reserves at risk of turning negative.
He said BNM, although not TH's regulator, had raised concerns about the impact of high profit distributions on the institution's already low reserves.
"Bank Negara Malaysia began raising concerns from 2014 over the impact of the practice of paying high profit distributions, which caused the already low reserves to become negative," he said when explaining the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH.
Zulkifli said BNM had sent five letters of warning to the TH chairman and the minister responsible for religious affairs at the time, highlighting the gap between TH's assets and liabilities.
"They were warned not once, not twice, not three times, but five times that the situation needed to be rectified immediately to ensure Tabung Haji did not breach the law."
He said the warnings were issued because failure to address the problem could have serious consequences for the country's financial stability.
The RCI found that TH's financial problems eventually worsened to the point where the asset-liability deficit exceeded RM10 billion in the fourth quarter of 2018, Zulkifli said.
The institution then faced the risk of large-scale withdrawals by depositors, while efforts to secure standby funding in case of a bank run had failed.
He said TH's entire deposits were guaranteed by the government, exposing the government to potential liabilities of about RM74.5 billion if the institution collapsed.
"The crisis was further highlighted by the findings of the Auditor General in the 2017 financial statements, including an emphasis-of-matter regarding changes to TH's impairment policy."
Zulkifli said the policy had been changed twice in the same year, allowing TH to report a higher profit for 2017.
Following the change of government in 2018, the new TH board appointed PwC to reassess the institution's financial position and performance according to applicable accounting standards.
"The review found that TH was facing a critical financial situation, prompting the government to implement a restructuring plan."
Zulkifli said the crisis demonstrated the consequences of failing to act on warnings about the institution's financial health.
"The warnings from Bank Negara Malaysia were not without basis. If they were not addressed, they risked causing serious consequences to the country's financial stability," he said.
The RCI has since recommended reforms to TH's governance, financial reporting and investment management, with more than 75 per cent of relevant recommendations already implemented, he added.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting today to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's explanation, followed by questions and debate from MPs.
The 211-page report, published on July 29, examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings were governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
The report found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) had been fully applied.

Title: Asean must protect vital sea lanes
Article:
LETTER:
IN an increasingly uncertain world, prudence — not power — is likely to be the region's greatest strategic asset besides robust domestic economic and security fundamentals.
Asean has survived well by not getting entangled in big power politics. However, the geopolitical environment in the region has shifted and lured some member states to err on the wrong side.
The rivalry between China and the United States for primacy in the South China Sea and over Taiwan has lately taken dangerous turns after emerging powers like Japan and Australia made separate defence deals with the Philippines, whose president is at odds with China.
The late Singaporean diplomat S. Rajaratnam once argued that Southeast Asia should avoid becoming an arena where major powers settle their rivalries. That insight remains remarkably relevant today.
While a united Asean possesses greater diplomatic leverage and centrality, a divided Asean becomes vulnerable to external pressures.
The maritime conflict in the Hormuz Strait can be replicated in Southeast Asia.
The region has several strategic straits used for international navigation that can be easily exploited by predatory powers.
Foremost are the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, which carry almost 30 per cent of global trade in oil, annually outpacing other energy corridors like the Hormuz Strait and Bab el-Mandeb.
Over 120,000 vessels pass through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore annually, making it the largest maritime oil transit chokepoint in the world.
The entire economic and security environment in the Indo-Pacific region can be devastated if access to both straits is blocked by predatory powers.
Apart from the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, there are other vital sea lanes in the region critical to international maritime navigation through the archipelagos of Indonesia and the Philippines that can be choked by unfriendly parties.
They include the Lombok Strait, Sunda Strait and Makassar Strait in Indonesia and the Philippines' three designated routes in the Philippines' archipelagic waters for international navigation, i.e., Balintang Channel, Sibutu Passage and Basilan Strait.
While serving as a lifeline for regional and global trade, the Straits of Malacca and Singapore are governed by a legal regime that permits unimpeded transit passage under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
Unlike Iran, all three littoral states — Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore — have ratified UNCLOS and have the obligation to ensure unimpeded free transit passage through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.
Asean's prosperity depends on open sea lanes, stable energy markets, predictable trade, and a rules-based international environment.
Asean's economic power comes as one market of nearly 700 million people and a US$3.9 trillion economy.
While the Asean single market is attractive, they invest in member countries that give them the best returns on their investment and meet their specific strategic goals.
While each member brings unique resources, skills, and geographic advantages that make the entire regional group resilient, balanced, and globally influential, the FDI is not spread equally in the region.
Between 50 and 70 per cent of capital flows in Asean go to Singapore.
This situation has created an element of inequality whose vulnerability can be exploited by predatory powers.
B.A. HAMZAH
Former Director-General,
Maritime Institute of Malaysia
