Title: Over 100 killed after strongest quake this century hits western Colombia
Article:
BOGOTA: More than 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, toppling buildings, damaging hospitals and infrastructure and trapping people beneath the rubble in the country's strongest earthquake this century.
The quake struck just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis, with memories still fresh of devastating twin earthquakes in neighbouring Venezuela in June.
"The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed," he said in a national address around 1 pm local time, upon declaring a national state of emergency and giving a death toll of 111.
"The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble."
De La Espriella visited Quibdo, the capital of coastal Choco province, where he promised rent subsidies for those who have lost homes, and then travelled to Cali, western Colombia's largest city.
Though he had been expected to give an updated national death toll on Monday evening, De La Espriella offered only figures for Valle del Cauca province, where Cali is located, saying 35 people had died there, while 700 had been injured.
Some local media have cited a national total of 132 deaths, though the origin of the figure is unclear.
The US Geological Survey said the 7.4-magnitude quake struck at a depth of 107 km.
Colombia's Geological Service said it was the strongest earthquake recorded in the country in the 21st century.
As night fell, rescue workers and volunteers with headlamps hurried to find people still trapped under rubble.
Authorities in Cali, Armenia and Manizales announced curfews, with Cali's mayor saying threats of looting had forced him to deploy police and military personnel to the streets.
De La Espriella promised 1,000 additional security personnel for the city.
Cali authorities said the Petronio Alvarez festival, an annual celebration of Pacific music which was due to start on Wednesday, has been postponed.
Video broadcast by Caracol Television showed a group of people pulling a small baby covered in dust from under a pile of rubble. Caracol reported the six-month-old girl and her mother were rescued from under a five-story building in Cali.
Video from Cali also showed rescue workers rappelling people out from the windows of a local hospital.
[[nid:1508672]]
In the hard-hit city of Pereira, rescue workers told local television they were in contact with a young boy trapped under a bakery, and crane operators were working to remove badly damaged parts of buildings.
A four-story building crumbled in Pereira during the quake, according to Reuters-verified video, while footage from Manizales showed one of the side towers of the city's landmark neo-Gothic cathedral collapsing and scattering debris onto nearby streets.
Reuters video showed rescue workers, police and volunteers shovelling debris by hand and loading rubble into trucks as they searched for survivors trapped beneath collapsed buildings.
Other footage showed damage to residential towers and emergency-service facilities, with debris crashing onto ambulances parked below.
Mauricio Andrade, a firefighter in Cali, said his team had rescued two adult women and two children from a collapsed building. As he spoke to Reuters, his team was preparing to rescue more people from the rubble.
"They are alive," he said. "We are making space so we can free them and get them out."
Carmen Yasmin Garcia, 43, a Cali resident and rescue volunteer, said her group had helped seven people out of a fallen building but there were still four people and a dog trapped underneath.
"A moment ago there was scratching but now we can't hear anything, we still have faith that the dog is alive and we can get these people out," she said.
"The more people lending a hand the better."
Saul Paz, 69, a resident of a Cali residential complex that partially collapsed, told Reuters he had been in the dining room with his son and wife when the shaking began.
"I think if it had lasted five seconds more there would be nothing left," he said. "There are people who went to bed last night with a house and a car and today they won't have anything."
Colombia's civil aviation authority suspended operations at several airports in the region, including Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, while engineers carried out structural inspections.

Title: Malaysia aims to be Asia-Pacific's most connected nation - Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airports aims to make Malaysia the most connected country in the Asia-Pacific, supported by capacity expansion at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and a push for more direct international routes.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the strategy would also strengthen direct connectivity to Penang, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching, rather than focusing solely on Kuala Lumpur.
"Today, Malaysia Airports has set itself the goal of making this nation the most connected country in the Asia-Pacific.
"This is backed by capacity expansion at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and a deliberate push to open direct routes to Penang, Kota Kinabalu and Kuching, not only to our capital," he said in his speech at the Think Business, Think Hong Kong symposium here today.
Loke said connectivity was essential to the movement of capital and goods, and would help deepen Malaysia's economic ties with major regional centres.
Citing Hong Kong as an example, he said Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong were less than four hours apart by air and shared the same time zone, while Cathay Pacific had added a fourth daily service between the two cities since March.
"There are four direct flights between Kuala Lumpur and Hong Kong just by Cathay Pacific. That has not included other airlines... and that tells us the commercial demand is real and still growing," he said.
He said KLIA already had a strategic collaboration with Henan Airport in Zhengzhou to develop a dual air cargo hub under the Air Silk Road concept, while there was potential for closer cooperation with Hong Kong International Airport.
"This is where KLIA and Hong Kong International Airport have a similar strength, and where we can create a dual hub between Asean and Hong Kong," he said.
Loke said Malaysia's aim was to position KLIA as a major cargo hub for the Asean region, complementing Hong Kong's strength as an East Asian aviation hub with links to markets including the United States and Canada.
"Our aim is to make KLIA our main cargo hub in the Asean region, while Hong Kong already has strength in East Asia and connecting to the US and Canada. And this is where both airports can work together very closely in terms of our air cargo throughput," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke urges Hong Kong investors to explore Malaysia beyond Klang Valley
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong investors should look beyond Kuala Lumpur and the Klang Valley when exploring investment opportunities in Malaysia, says Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
Loke said the government is adopting a multi-pronged strategy to spread economic growth nationwide, with regions offering distinct opportunities in semiconductors, renewable energy, and tourism.
"When you look at Malaysia, do not just focus on Kuala Lumpur, the Klang Valley, and Selangor, which are the hub for our trade and finance.
"The Malaysian government is adopting a multi-growth-area strategy, where throughout the peninsula we have multiple areas for growth," he said at the Think Business, Think Hong Kong symposium today.
Present were Hong Kong Trade Development Council chairman Prof Frederick Ma and Hong Kong Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau.
In the north, Loke identified Penang and Kulim in Kedah as key corridors for semiconductors and electronics that continue to attract global investment.
In the south, he highlighted Johor as a major growth area following the establishment of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, which capitalises on proximity to Singapore.
On the east coast, Loke said the 665km East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), a major Belt and Road Initiative project connecting the region to the Klang Valley, will serve as a catalyst for manufacturing, with its first phase expected to be completed next year.
For East Malaysia, Loke said Sarawak offers vast potential in renewable and green energy, while Sabah presents opportunities in tourism and the blue economy.
"So there are multiple locations, multiple areas, multiple industries that we can look at in Malaysia.
"We hope that investors from Hong Kong can examine Malaysia more thoroughly," he said.
Loke said Malaysia's future development direction was also set out under the New Industrial Master Plan 2030, with the country seeking to move further up the value chain into advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, the digital economy and the energy transition.
"We have also become more selective about the investment we court, because the objective now is quality and long-term capability rather than headline figures," he added.
The symposium today brought together business leaders from Hong Kong and Malaysia for dialogue, networking, business matching and one-on-one consultations aimed at strengthening commercial ties between the two economies.
More than 200 government and business leaders, start-up entrepreneurs and professional service providers from Hong Kong attended the event, representing the largest Hong Kong delegation to the symposium to date.

Title: Lim Guan Eng says six proposals to help MSMEs rejected by govt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today said six measures he proposed to help micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) cope with rising costs and economic pressures had been rejected by the government.
In a Facebook post today, the Bagan MP said he had presented the proposals to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during a meeting on July 20, including raising the annual turnover threshold for e-Invoicing to RM5 million.
The other proposals were to establish a special taxpayers’ tribunal for individuals and MSMEs, abolish the two per cent Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contribution by employers for foreign workers, and streamline foreign worker approvals through comprehensive digital and online processing.
He also proposed a one-year moratorium on interest payments for existing MSME loans, as well as RM5 billion in interest-free and collateral-free financing for 100,000 MSMEs, capped at RM50,000 per business.
Lim said the measures were necessary to ensure the survival of 1.1 million MSMEs in Malaysia, which he said contributed 38 per cent to the country’s gross domestic product (GDP), accounted for 48 per cent of employment and nearly 13 per cent of total exports.
He also said the banking industry should play a greater role in supporting MSMEs, pointing to an increase in pre-tax profits in the sector from RM48.3 billion in 2024 to RM54.8 billion last year.
Lim said the six proposals were rejected in a July 23 letter from Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican in response to his earlier letter to Anwar dated April 8.
However, the letter did not expressly state that the proposals had been rejected, saying instead that the Finance Ministry would examine them comprehensively, taking into account the government’s financial position, current policy priorities and the potential multiplier effects on the economy.
The ministry also said the government had already implemented several measures to support MSMEs affected by rising operating costs, including RM5 billion in guarantees under the Business Financing Guarantee Company (SJPP).
It said the implementation of Phase Four of e-Invoicing for businesses with annual sales of between RM1 million and RM5 million had been postponed until December 31, 2027.
The ministry also said it was considering an import duty exemption for the re-importation of Malaysian-made goods that could not complete the export process due to disruptions caused by the conflict in West Asia, until December 31 this year.
Johan said the government remained committed to ensuring the MSME ecosystem remained resilient and able to adapt to changing circumstances, adding that Lim’s proposals would be assessed based on their suitability and effectiveness in improving government policies.

Title: King orders full probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has ordered a comprehensive and transparent investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
The Star
reported that Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Zulkifli Hasan said the King had instructed that the investigation be conducted without compromise, with no stone left unturned.
“His Majesty’s concern underscores the importance of safeguarding the trust and confidence of Muslims in the country’s Haj management and Islamic financial institutions, which is in line with the Madani government’s commitment,” he said during the tabling of the report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Zulkifli said the Cabinet had unanimously reviewed the RCI report on July 29 and decided to make it public by tabling and debating it during the special parliamentary sitting.
“The Cabinet has also agreed for a full investigation to be conducted immediately by the enforcement authorities based on the RCI findings.
“Following the decision, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police acted swiftly by launching follow-up investigations and arresting several key individuals linked to alleged misconduct highlighted in the RCI report,” he said.
Zulkifli said the actions demonstrated the government’s and enforcement authorities’ continued commitment to ensuring there would be no compromise against any party involved in abuse of power or criminal breach of trust involving assets and funds belonging to the country’s Haj pilgrims.

Title: BNM issued five warning letters to Tabung Haji leadership over asset-liability gap
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) had issued five warning letters to the Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and the Minister of Religious Affairs regarding the gap between TH’s assets and liabilities.
The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs  Zulkifli Hasan, said that TH’s management had been warned that the situation needed to be rectified immediately to ensure TH does not continue to be in violation of the law.
“At the time, TH’s position posed a potential systemic risk to the country’s financial stability. Unfortunately, those letters were ignored by TH’s leadership,” he said.
He said this during a ministerial briefing on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH, as well as the efforts and measures taken to restore the institution’s financial position, at a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today.
Zulkifli added that BNM’s warnings were followed by a reprimand from the Auditor-General in the 2017 Financial Statements Report.
He said the Auditor-General had issued an Emphasis of Matter on changes to the impairment policy, which were made twice in the same year to show higher profits for 2017.
“Following the reprimand from the authorities, TH’s new board appointed the international audit firm PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) in 2018 to reassess TH’s financial position and performance in accordance with valid and accurate accounting standards,” he added.
Subsequently, financial manipulation was confirmed by PwC in its report, which found that only RM556 million of the total assets of RM4.6 billion were valued by professional valuers.
On July 29, the 211-page RCI report was made public, containing various findings on weaknesses in the institution’s management and operations during the 2014-2020 period.
The report also included 25 recommendations for improvement, 75 per cent of which had been implemented by TH as of July 30.
The government announced the establishment of the RCI in 2021, followed by the appointment of its members on Jan 20, 2022. The report was subsequently presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Aug 30, 2022. — Bernama

Title: Two men with combined 52 criminal records nabbed over Jasin KK Mart robbery
Article:
JASIN, Aug 11 — Police have arrested two men believed to be involved in an armed robbery at a KK Mart convenience store in Taman Maju here on Aug 6.
Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said the two suspects, aged 44 and 45, were arrested separately at about 4.30 pm yesterday.
He said the first suspect was arrested by the roadside along Jalan PPJ 3 in Jasin town, while the second was arrested in Sagil, Tangkak, Johor.
“The first suspect admitted to riding a motorcycle and waiting outside the premises, while the second suspect entered the KK Mart to commit the robbery,” he said in a statement today.
Police also seized several items believed to be linked to the case, including three mobile phones, clothing and shoes believed to have been worn by the suspects, two helmets, a paper cutter knife and a KTM Duke 200 motorcycle.
He said the first suspect had 22 previous criminal records, while the second, who is under the supervision of the Tangkak District Police Headquarters, had 30 previous records.
The case is being investigated under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery with the use of a weapon.
Both suspects will be brought before the Jasin Magistrate’s Court today for a remand application. — Bernama

Title: NEEAP 2.0 targets RM85.24b savings, 11.6 per cent reduction in energy demand by 2035
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The National Energy Efficiency Policy and Action Plan 2026–2035 (NEEAP 2.0) aims to deliver RM85.24 billion in utility savings, reduce national energy demand by 11.6 per cent, and achieve cumulative energy savings of 815,383 terajoules (TJ) by 2035.
The policy and action plan also include a greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions avoidance of 26,108 kilotonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂eq).
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who officiated the launch of the NEEAP 2.0 here today, said the plan is guided by the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act 2024.
“The Act marks an important shift towards institutionalising efficiency across our economy.
“Together with the next phase of national policy, including thermal energy management, it will encourage users to optimise consumption, improve competitiveness and reduce pressure on the grid,” he said in his speech at the 7th International Sustainable Energy Summit (ISES 2026).
He said that over ten years, the NEEAP 1.0 delivered electricity savings of 60,886 gigawatt-hours, exceeding its target of 52,233 gigawatt-hours.
“This is equivalent to an estimated GHG reduction totalling 35.6 million tonnes and savings of approximately RM16.1 billion,” said Akmal Nasrullah.
He opined that energy efficiency must become standard business practice and a national productivity tool, and ultimately, a way of life.
The NEEAP 2.0 focused on four strategic thrusts, namely, implementation of energy efficiency (EE) plan; reskilling and upskilling the workforce for operational EE improvement; sustainable funding mechanisms; and facilitating private sector EE initiatives and investments.
Key initiatives include improving EE across the industrial, building and domestic sectors through measures such as energy-efficient facilities, energy audits, and regulating new equipment and appliances.
The plan is in line with key roadmaps in Malaysia, namely the National Energy Policy 2022–2040, National Energy Transition Roadmap, New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the 12th and 13th Malaysia Plan.
It was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, ministries, government agencies, industry associations, key industry players, experts and related stakeholders.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) said that the implementation of NEEAP 2.0 is expected to attract RM36 billion in private investment and create approximately 29,000 new jobs.
Building upon the achievements of the previous action plan, NEEAP 2.0 will drive the nation’s energy transition towards the aspiration of net-zero emissions by 2050 by fostering a culture of EE across the industrial, commercial, and domestic sectors, it said.
“Priority will continue to be given to high-impact sectors to stimulate the country’s economic growth, while ensuring the participation of all segments of the society,” the ministry said.
PETRA added that the estimated cumulative energy saving of 815,000 TJ is equivalent to the energy required to meet the entire electricity supply needs of Peninsular Malaysia for nearly two years. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Perikatan neglecting Tabung Haji depositors after MPs walk out of RCI debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today slammed the opposition, accusing it of trying to divert attention from issues involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) by making him the subject of political polemics.
He said the focus should instead be on those he described as “betrayers” of TH and the interests of the institution’s depositors, rather than making him the target of the debate.
“Do you want to debate about me or Tabung Haji? Do you want to know about me or the betrayal of Tabung Haji?
“Malay Muslims have been betrayed, yet there are still those who want to engage in political drama? What more when it comes from those who constantly champion Malay and Muslim causes,” he said in a Facebook post this afternoon.
He also questioned the position taken by Perikatan Nasional (PN), which is anchored by PAS, particularly over the interests of TH depositors from various walks of life.
“Does PN, which is anchored by PAS, not care about the interests of ordinary people — fishermen, farmers, teachers, police, soldiers and retirees — who work hard to save money in Tabung Haji to fulfil the fifth pillar of Islam?” he asked.
The post came after several opposition MPs walked out of the Dewan Rakyat and did not participate in this morning’s special sitting to discuss the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH.
The opposition MPs were reportedly unhappy with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul’s decision to proceed with the briefing in the absence of the Prime Minister and reject a proposal by PN chief whip Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan for the sitting to be postponed.
Anwar had earlier apologised for being unable to attend the special sitting as he was undergoing physiotherapy following an elective laparoscopic procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia.
Today’s special Dewan Rakyat sitting was held to hear the Minister’s briefing on the RCI report on TH, as well as the efforts and measures taken to restore the institution’s financial position.
On July 29, the 211-page RCI report was made public, containing various findings on weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, as well as 25 recommendations for improvement, of which 75 per cent had been implemented by TH as of July 30.
The government announced the establishment of the RCI in 2021, followed by the appointment of its members on Jan 20, 2022. The RCI subsequently presented its report to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on Aug 30, 2022.

Title: Govt’s over RM10b Tabung Haji bailout aimed at restoring finances, not taking over assets, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government rescued Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) through a bailout exceeding RM10 billion due to mismanagement and embezzlement, to restore its financial position and not to take over the institution’s assets, the Dewan Rakyat was informed today.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Zulkifli Hasan, also emphasised that no assets were sold to non-Muslims or Chinese, as falsely claimed by some irresponsible parties seeking to incite hatred and provoke the public.
The assets are owned by Urusharta Jamaah, a wholly-owned company of the Minister of Finance Incorporated, he noted.
He said this during the minister’s briefing session on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH and the efforts and actions taken to restore the financial position of the institution at the Special Sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said TH is facing a critical situation where the deficit gap between TH’s assets and liabilities has widened to over RM10 billion in the fourth quarter of 2018, with only three months to find a solution.
“At that time, TH was insolvent and needed to be rescued. The situation ultimately forced the Pakatan Harapan Government to bail out TH with a restructuring plan to restore its financial position so that TH could become solvent again and remain sustainable in the long term,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji launches booklet to explain RCI findings, to restore depositors’ confidence
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 (Bernama) -- Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) today launched a major public enlightenment initiative on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH through the distribution of a special information booklet.
The booklet, titled “Tabung Haji: Apa Sudah Jadi?” (Tabung Haji: What Happened?), is aimed at enabling the public to obtain accurate and transparent facts directly from official sources, thereby dispelling confusion regarding management malpractices from 2014 to 2020 as highlighted in the RCI report released publicly last month.
The move is also to restore the confidence of more than nine million depositors in the sustainability and future governance of the country’s haj management institution through verified facts.
The initiative is being implemented through the distribution of posters in both digital and printed formats, allowing the public to examine the contents and actual findings of the investigation in greater depth and accuracy.
To ensure wider access to the information, the digital booklet were distributed directly to mosques and suraus via the WhatsApp application today, while printed versions will be distributed on Friday (Aug 14), especially around the Federal Territory.
The booklet, which summarises the original 211-page document, details the chronology that led to the inquiry, beginning with warnings issued by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) between 2014 and 2015 regarding TH’s weak and risky financial position.
Through the booklet, TH also highlighted several critical findings of the RCI, including the institution’s failure to manage the asset-liability deficit it had been experiencing since 2014, as well as confirmation that laws and accounting standards had been breached.
It also details the issue invlolving use of Realisable Asset Value (RAV) for the purpose of declaring hibah (profit distribution), with the method found not to be a recognised accounting standard in the preparation of financial statements.
In addition, the booklet openly addresses governance issues and the risk of political interference, weaknesses in investment monitoring, and conflicts of interest involving subsidiaries, which were among the factors contributing to the shortcomings.
However, the RCI affirmed that the 2018 TH Recovery and Restructuring Plan was the most appropriate and critical measure taken to save and restore TH’s financial position.
The concise booklet also outlines several key RCI recommendations to safeguard TH’s future, including a proposal to strengthen the Tabung Haji Act to streamline the organisation’s power structure, functions and governance, as well as a ban on the appointment of active politicians as chairman or board members.
Following the implementation of most of the recommendations, TH also shared the latest developments in its financial position which is now at a very strong level, including its success in announcing a 3.5 per cent profit distribution for 2025, the highest in eight years.
To date, depositors’ funds have shown an encouraging upward trend, reaching RM93.4 billion, while TH recorded investment income of RM4.64 billion in 2025, the highest figure in its history.
TH’s improving integrity has also seen the agency pay RM693.6 million in zakat for the period from 2019 to 2025, in addition to continuing to gain international recognition through the Diamond Award (Best Overall) at the Labbaytum Awards by Saudi Arabia for 2025 and 2026.
To date, over 75 per cent of the RCI recommendations have been and are being implemented by TH
This enlightenment initiative was launched on the same day a special Dewan Rakyat sitting was held to debate the RCI report in detail. — Bernama

Title: Zulkifli: Tabung Haji now in much stronger position after institutional recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is now in a much stronger position after undergoing an institutional recovery process, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
He said that when the Madani government took over the administration of the country at the end of 2022, TH was in the process of addressing legacy assets that were less competitive and problematic, which had remained in the institution since 2018.
“The government chose to give TH room to restore the institution first. Today, with TH in a much stronger position, we have chosen to make this report available to the people.
“Alhamdulillah, the government wishes to express its highest appreciation to the new TH management and all parties involved who have restored TH to excellent health,” he said.
He said this during the ministerial briefing session on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Tabung Haji and the efforts and measures taken to restore the institution’s financial position, at the Special Dewan Rakyat Sitting today.
Zulkifli said TH had also received five World’s Best Haj Management Awards over four consecutive years, demonstrating that capable, competent, trustworthy and integrity-driven leadership could steer the institution effectively.
He said the Cabinet, on July 29, unanimously agreed to make the RCI report public and table and debate it for the first time through a special Parliament sitting, while also ordering a full investigation to be carried out immediately by enforcement agencies.
Following the decision, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and police began investigations and detained several key individuals linked to the misappropriation mentioned in the report.
“This firm action demonstrates the government’s and enforcement agencies’ continued commitment that there will be no compromise for any party involved in abuse of power or criminal breach of trust involving the assets and sacred funds belonging to the country’s pilgrims,” he said.
Zulkifli said the action was in line with the decree of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, that investigations into the RCI findings be conducted comprehensively, transparently and without any compromise, “until every stone is turned”.
On the trust placed in TH, he said deposits in the institution included money gradually saved by parents for their children, as well as savings belonging to teachers, small traders, retirees, farmers, fishermen, rubber tappers and taxi drivers.
“They do not save merely to pursue profits. They save because they want to reach the Baitullah.
“That is why, when a trust of this magnitude is compromised, we cannot hide behind the figures. We cannot sweep it under the carpet. And we cannot allow narratives driven by political interests to override the interests of depositors and the Muslim community,” he said.
Zulkifli said every decision involving TH must be guided by the principles of trust and depositors’ confidence, while any questions regarding a breach of trust must be investigated to establish the truth, rectify weaknesses and ensure the same issues do not recur, which was the spirit behind the establishment of the RCI.
The RCI, announced by the previous government in 2021, was chaired by former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Raus Sharif and comprised five prominent figures with expertise in public administration, banking, finance, syariah and accounting. Its members were appointed on Jan 20, 2022, before the report was presented to the King on Aug 30 of the same year.
On July 29, the 211-page RCI report was made public, containing various findings on weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020. It also put forward 25 recommendations for improvement, of which 75 per cent had been implemented as of July 30, while the remaining relevant recommendations are being actively implemented. — Bernama

Title: Police: 14-year-old girl arrested after allegedly injuring classmate with kerambit in Shah Alam
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 11 — Police today confirmed that a 14-year-old female student was arrested after allegedly injuring a classmate with a sharp object at a secondary school in Shah Alam.
Shah Alam police chief Assistant Commissioner Sarudin Samah said the suspect had brought a kerambit and injured a male classmate with it at around 11.42am on August 5.
“An arrest was subsequently made and the case is currently under investigation,” he said, confirming that a police report had been lodged.
Sarudin said the victim sustained minor injuries to the arm, adding that no motive had been established for the incident.
He added that the victim was in stable condition, while the suspect had been released on police bail.
The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means.

Title: Govt could have faced RM74.5b liability from Tabung Haji bank run in 2018, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government risked assuming liabilities of about RM74.5 billion if a massive panic withdrawal, or “bank run”, had occurred in 2018, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
He noted that a panic withdrawal did occur in 2019, involving net withdrawals of RM6 billion within a short period following the announcement of a 1.25 per cent hibah for 2018 in early 2019.
“Imagine if no hibah had been declared. How much panic withdrawal could have occurred?” he said during a ministerial briefing on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH), as well as the efforts and measures taken to restore the institution’s financial position, at a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said that technically, TH was insolvent at the time and needed to be rescued, forcing the Pakatan Harapan government to step in with a restructuring plan aimed at restoring TH’s financial position, allowing the institution to return to solvency and remain financially sustainable in the long term. — Bernama

Title: Akmal Nasrullah: Malaysia’s renewable energy transition to catalyse RM4.3b investment, create 7,738 jobs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Malaysia’s renewable energy transition is expected to catalyse about RM4.3 billion in investments and create approximately 7,738 indirect employment opportunities through 42 projects approved under the 2026 Feed-in Tariff (FiT) e-bidding exercise, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today.
He said the projects, involving biogas, biomass and small hydropower, would also generate about RM617 million in demand for locally manufactured gas engines and boilers.
“This is the outcome we seek: more renewable energy, stronger domestic supply chains, greater investment and tangible economic value for the country.
“Every ringgit invested in the transition should strengthen Malaysian capabilities. It should deepen local supply chains, create skilled employment, support innovation and build Malaysian enterprises that can compete across ASEAN,” he said.
Akmal said the Sustainable Energy Development Authority (SEDA) Malaysia had received 48 applications under the 2026 FiT e-bidding exercise, with 42 successfully awarded a combined approved net export capacity of 331.355 megawatts.
The successful projects comprise 16 biogas projects totalling 26.185MW, 11 biomass projects totalling 135.94MW and 15 small hydropower projects totalling 169.23MW.
Speaking at the 7th International Sustainable Energy Summit (ISES) 2026 here, Akmal said the approved projects were expected to enter the system between 2029 and 2030, taking into account construction and other project delivery requirements.
He later clarified to reporters that the electricity generated by the projects would be for domestic use rather than export.
Akmal said the FiT mechanism would also help Malaysia diversify its renewable energy sources by incorporating biomass, biogas and small hydropower into the country’s energy mix.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir (center) interacts with exhibitors while visiting the Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) booth during the 7th International Sustainable Energy Summit (ISES) 2026. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
“For Malaysia, energy transition is economic policy. It shapes where companies invest, how industries compete, the quality of jobs we create and the resilience of our households,” he said.
He said Malaysia’s economy was estimated to have expanded by 5.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, bringing first-half growth to 5.6 per cent.
Akmal said this provided a strong foundation for implementation of the 13th Malaysia Plan, which targets annual gross domestic product growth of between 4.5 and 5.5 per cent from 2026 to 2030.
Under the National Energy Transition Roadmap, Malaysia is targeting renewable energy to account for 70 per cent of installed capacity by 2050, with an interim target of 35 per cent by 2030.
Akmal said achieving the targets would require investment in renewable energy generation, the electricity grid, energy storage, technology and skills.
He said the government’s approach must ensure sufficient and reliable energy, support a competitive and lower-carbon economy, and ensure the benefits and costs of the transition were shared fairly.
The two-day ISES 2026, themed “Envisioning Sustainable Energy Beyond Borders”, brings together policymakers, industry leaders, investors, financial institutions, researchers and energy experts to discuss regional energy cooperation, grid flexibility, energy storage, sustainable finance, energy efficiency and renewable energy.

Title: Opposition walks out after Speaker rejects deferment of special Tabung Haji RCI sitting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Opposition lawmakers walked out almost immediately after today’s special parliamentary sitting on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji convened.
Earlier, Kota Bharu MP Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the sitting should be deferred until the prime minister recovers and resumes his duties.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is currently undergoing physiotherapy treatment after undergoing an elective laparoscopic surgery procedure to treat a para-umbilical hernia.
“if we debate without the prime minister, it is just as good as doing a press conference,” Takiyuddin, who is also the Opposition’s chief whip, told the Dewan Rakyat today.
“The Speaker himself confirmed that the status of today’s sitting is only a ministerial briefing. The government has also confirmed that there will be no voting today,” he added.
Meanwhile, Arau MP Datuk Seri Shahidan Kassim questioned why the RCI report did not include clarifications from Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng when the investigation covered between 2014 to 2020.
Lim served as the finance minister in the first Pakatan Harapan government from May 2018 to February 2020.
A commotion briefly ensued between Shahidan and Hulu Langat MP Mohd Sany Hamzan, when the latter intervened to stress that the sitting should proceed as scheduled.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul later clarified that the sitting will proceed in line with Standing Order 11(3) and that deputy prime minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and other Cabinet ministers were present in Anwar’s absence to represent the government.
During a separate press conference with PN lawmakers later, Takiyuddin also questioned why the report was not tabled and debated in the Parliament before it was declassified for the public.
He said PN had already submitted a letter to the Speaker’s office yesterday requesting for the postponement.
Meanwhile, Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin questioned Anwar’s rationale of disclosing the report now after withholding it for years on the grounds that it could erode the confidence of the Malays.
When asked if Bersatu would also join the walkout, Hamzah said: “I don’t know about that. This was discussed among us (Pas and Parti Wawasan Negara).
At the time of writing, Bersatu lawmakers were still present in Dewan Rakyat.

Title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker confirms Wong Chen’s resignation as Subang MP, says EC notified of vacancy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul today confirmed Wong Chen’s resignation as Subang MP.
He said that he has informed the Election Commissions (EC) regarding the matter.
“As everyone is aware, the Honourable Member for Subang has submitted a letter to me to relinquish his membership, effective yesterday, as a Member of the Dewan Rakyat.
“I have informed the EC of the vacancy in the Subang parliamentary seat in accordance with Article 54(1) of the Federal Constitution” he said before the start of the special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today.
Wong Chen on August 5 said that he had met up with Johari to hand over his resignation letter, allowing parliamentary officers three working days to prepare for the vacancy.
The three-term PKR MP also said that his team will be removing the honorific title of Yang Berhormat from all their billboards, signages and correspondence by next month.
Wong Chen is expected to hold a press conference tomorrow at 11am.

Title: Man arrested after trying to open Batik Air emergency door at 9,144m on flight from Malaysia to India
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A man was arrested after allegedly attempting to open an emergency exit door while travelling on a Batik Air flight from Malaysia to India at an altitude of about 9,144 metres.
According to People, the 36-year-old suspect, identified as Jamsheer Athanikkal, allegedly behaved erratically during the flight, which had departed from Malaysia for India recently.
An Indian Express report quoted a police officer as saying the incident occurred between 9.30pm and 11pm local time, with Jamsheer seated in 12A, Kosmo! Online reported.
“Without any provocation, he tried to open the emergency exit door and damaged the window panel.
“He also threatened other passengers and crew members who tried to stop him,” the officer said.
Video footage of the incident shared on social media showed several crew members restraining Jamsheer with zip ties.
He was arrested after the aircraft landed at Kochi International Airport on suspicion of criminal intimidation, failure to comply with safety instructions and endangering public safety.
Asked about his motive, Jamsheer reportedly told police that he acted because he suddenly felt like doing so.
