Title: Man dies after car carrying rice sacks crashes into ditch in Tanah Merah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A 39-year-old man died after the Proton Wira he was driving, which was carrying sacks of rice, skidded and overturned into a ditch along the East-West Highway in Kampung Batu 9, Batang Merbau in Tanah Merah, Kelantan, last night.
Kemahang Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Mat Nuri Muhamad said the department received an emergency call via NG999 at 11.44pm, according to
Sinar Harian
.
He said firefighters arrived at the scene at 11.50pm and found the Proton Wira overturned in the ditch.
“The Malay male driver, aged 39, was trapped in the driver’s seat.
“Firefighters used hydraulic cutting equipment to extricate the victim before handing him over to medical personnel,” he said in a statement today.
Mat Nuri said the victim was pronounced dead at the scene and his remains were handed over to police for further action.
He said the operation, which involved five firefighters, ended at 12.28am.

Title: Anwar thanks well-wishers, to follow special Parliament sitting on Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has thanked everyone who prayed for his wellbeing and sent him birthday wishes as he turns 79 today.
The Prime Minister’s Office said Anwar’s health was improving and that he would continue undergoing physiotherapy under the supervision of a team of medical specialists.
Anwar also apologised for being unable to attend the special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat today to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji from 2014 to 2020.
“He will follow the debate closely to ensure that the institution entrusted with the affairs of Muslims continues to be safeguarded,” said Anwar’s senior press secretary Tunku Nashrul Abaidah in a statement today.
Anwar also prayed for the smooth conduct of the special sitting.

Title: Rafizi: Govt has yet to fully settle RM12.5b Tabung Haji commitment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — The government has yet to fully settle its RM12.5 billion financial commitment to Lembaga Tabung Haji following the maturity of a Sukuk Urusan Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) instrument in May, former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said.
In a statement on Facebook last night, Rafizi said only RM965 million of the RM12.5 billion owed to Tabung Haji had been settled through property assets, while the remaining RM11.5 billion was replaced with another sukuk that will mature in 2036.
He said the property assets comprised a plot of land at the Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) and plantation land in Sarawak.
“The Sukuk UJSB Series 1 matured on May 29, 2026.
“Properly, the government should settle its commitment to fully redeem the RM12.5 billion owed to Tabung Haji, either in cash or equivalent assets,” the statement read.
Rafizi said the financial restructuring of Tabung Haji approved by the government in late 2018 involved the federal government, through wholly owned company Urusan Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB), taking over loss-making Tabung Haji assets at values higher than their actual worth.
In return, UJSB issued two series of sukuk to Tabung Haji, with the federal government required to redeem the instruments upon maturity in 2026 and 2029, either in cash or assets at recovered value.
He said the arrangement was intended as a temporary measure to restore Tabung Haji’s reserves to positive levels and allow it to continue paying returns to depositors.
Rafizi said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Tabung Haji’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, particularly pages 107 to 137, highlighted the need for the government to make annual budget allocations to fulfil its commitments when the sukuk matured.
He said the Pakatan Harapan, Perikatan Nasional and current administrations had approved allocations for the redemption of the UJSB sukuk since 2019.
Rafizi said the government under then prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad approved at least RM17.8 billion on April 5, 2019 to cover the shortfall in the redemption of UJSB sukuk, with the commitment subsequently carried forward under the 12th Malaysia Plan during Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob’s administration.
He claimed that only RM500 million had so far been paid to Tabung Haji to redeem the UJSB sukuk, citing the RCI’s findings.
He also said the RM1.5 billion approved under Budget 2021 during the Perikatan Nasional administration was not paid to Tabung Haji, with the government at the time citing the need to support economic recovery following the Covid-19 pandemic.
“Therefore, tomorrow’s parliamentary debate should receive a clear explanation from the government on where the billions allocated over the years to restore Tabung Haji have gone,” he said yesterday.
Rafizi said repeatedly deferring the government’s commitment by replacing one debt instrument with another could leave Tabung Haji facing liquidity and cash-flow risks in the future.
The Dewan Rakyat will hold a special sitting today to debate the RCI report on Tabung Haji’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, which was made public on July 29.

Title: Three Malaysians detained in Taiwan over alleged scam mule activities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Three Malaysians were detained in Kaohsiung, Taiwan last month for allegedly acting as money mules for a scam syndicate.
Central News Agency (CNA) reported yesterday that the three male suspects, aged 18, 26 and 39, entered Taiwan as tourists before being detained separately, according to
Berita Harian
.
According to the report, Zuoying Police detained the 18- and 39-year-old suspects at several locations, including while they were making withdrawals at post office automated teller machines (ATMs).
The 39-year-old suspect was reportedly detained in front of a post office ATM, with police seizing NT$155,000 (RM19,050) in cash, two bank cards and a mobile phone.
The 18-year-old suspect was also detained in front of a post office ATM, with NT$60,000 in cash, a bank card and a mobile phone found in his possession.
The 26-year-old suspect was detained at Kaohsiung International Airport in mid-July in an operation involving Taiwan’s National Immigration Agency and Aviation Police Bureau.
Police seized NT$2,800 in cash and two mobile phones from the suspect.
The three Malaysians were among four foreign nationals detained by Zuoying Police in operations conducted between late June and July.
The Ciaotou District Court subsequently ordered all the suspects to be detained pending further investigation.
CNA quoted police as saying scam syndicates were increasingly recruiting foreigners to enter Taiwan as tourists and act as money mules.
Most reportedly stayed for about a week before leaving Taiwan after completing cash withdrawals on behalf of the syndicate.
The tactic is believed to be used to break the trail and make it more difficult for authorities to track the suspects.

Title: Seven-year-old boy feared drowned after falling into river in Subang Jaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A seven-year-old Indonesian boy is feared drowned after falling into a river at Persiaran Subang Indah, near a supermarket in Subang Jaya, last night.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Assistant Director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 8.06 pm.
He said a team from the Subang Jaya Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene and arrived 10 minutes later.
“Based on the initial report from the Operations Commander, the victim is believed to have fallen into the river at about 6.30 pm while playing with his friends,” he said in a statement.
According to him, the search and rescue operation using surface-water search methods around the area was facing challenges due to the relatively strong river current.
“The Water Rescue Team from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station has also been called in to assist with the search operation,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Mindef channels RM275.4m to MAF veterans’ welfare programmes this year
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 11 — The Ministry of Defence (Mindef) has channeled RM275.4 million, or 90 per cent, of the RM303.3 million allocated to the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) to the Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV) this year.
In a press release yesterday, Mindef said the funding will cover five main focus areas of welfare, health, housing, education and socioeconomic empowerment.
The statement revealed that under the welfare focus, several initiatives have been carried out as of June. These include expanding cost-of-living assistance from 15,000 to 33,655 recipients, providing medical equipment and disaster relief to over 281 veterans, and funeral management support to more than 1,600 veterans.
In addition, MINDEF has prioritised the health and well-being of veterans, benefiting over 4,738 recipients with expenditures exceeding RM38 million as of June.
The ministry has also approved 34 new home construction projects and 323 home repair projects for MAF veterans to date.
Mindef also confirmed that education support for veterans’ children will continue. This includes school assistance and help for those entering higher education institutions.
The ministry is also focusing on veteran socioeconomic empowerment through various strategic partnerships, which include the Veteran Entrepreneur Empowerment Programme (PUVET) MAF Master Class, IPR INTAN Programme in Kuala Kubu Bharu, MyHero Tani Programme, and second-career opportunities under the Veteran MyWira Programme, PROWIRA-RTW Graduate Programme, and Work-Based Learning initiatives.
Mindef reiterated its commitment to honouring the service and sacrifices of MAF veterans, aiming to enhance their well-being as part of a broader effort to build a holistic and sustainable national defence ecosystem.
In a related development, Mindef highlighted the Madani Veteran Care Programme (PVM) in Merlimau, organised by JHEV.
The programme is designed to reach out to veterans and gain a closer understanding of their living conditions in the area.
It was attended by Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari and JHEV deputy director-general Sophian Isswandy Ismail.
During the programme, the team visited 15 homes belonging to MAF veterans, widows of veterans, and families with spouses or children with disabilities.
These visits served both to assess the veterans’ circumstances and to deliver targeted assistance based on individual needs, including home repairs, medical equipment, cost-of-living aid and daily essentials.
The programme also acted as a two-way engagement platform, helping to strengthen ties between the ministry and the veteran community.
Feedback gathered during these visits will be used to refine and improve future policies and welfare programmes. — Bernama

Title: Sri Aman forest fire spreads to 100ha, feared to worsen Sarawak haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — A forest fire in Sri Aman has spread across about 100 hectares, raising concerns that it could worsen haze conditions in Sarawak as air quality deteriorates due to transboundary smoke.
A spokesperson for the Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said the fire, which started around noon yesterday, had spread across about 100 hectares of forest along Jalan Kejatau-Lingga, Sri Aman, according to a
Harian Metro
report.
He said the department received a call about the incident at 1.19pm before a team from the Sri Aman Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene to conduct firefighting operations.
“The operations team arrived at the location at 1.35pm and began firefighting operations with seven personnel.
“The operation used an open water source from a ditch and also received water supplies from Rural Water Supply Department (JBALB) tanker lorries, as well as a tanker from the Betong Fire and Rescue Station, which supplied water to the fire engine’s tank,” he said in a statement last night.
Firefighters also created firebreaks to prevent the flames from spreading to other areas.
“The firefighting efforts were also assisted by an excavator from the Sri Aman Drainage and Irrigation Department (JPS) to help contain the fire.
“When operations were halted at 7.50pm, about 20 hectares of the total 100 hectares of affected area had been extinguished, while the remaining 80 hectares had not been fully extinguished,” he said.
He said operations would resume tomorrow due to darkness, insufficient lighting and a lack of water sources at the location.
“Among the challenges faced by the operations team were the lack of communication coverage, strong winds that caused the fire to spread rapidly, limited open water sources such as ditches, as well as narrow roads that made it difficult for firefighting vehicles to move,” he said.
Sri Aman was among the locations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with a reading of 114 as of 9pm last night.

Title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as 11 areas record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Haze conditions in Sarawak have worsened, with the number of areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising to 11 as of 6am today.
Based on information displayed on the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) website, the Serian IPD monitoring station recorded the sharpest increase, with an API reading of 189, approaching the very unhealthy level,
Harian Metro
reported.
Besides Serian, 10 other monitoring stations also recorded API readings in the unhealthy category.
The areas were Samarahan (171), Kuching (166), Bintulu (159), Samalaju (156) and Mukah (155).
Ibu also recorded an API reading of 154, followed by Sarikei (153), Sri Aman (152), Miri (135) and the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (111).
Two other stations recorded moderate readings but were edging closer to the unhealthy level, namely Limbang (81) and Kapit (73).
The development indicates that air quality in several parts of Sarawak is deteriorating, particularly with readings increasing at several key locations.
API readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy, while readings between 201 and 300 are considered very unhealthy.
Such conditions can affect health, particularly among vulnerable groups such as children, senior citizens and those with respiratory problems or chronic illnesses.
The public is therefore advised to monitor the latest air quality developments and reduce outdoor activities if haze conditions worsen.

Title: Ahmad Zahid visits Ismail Sabri at IJN, prays for former PM’s recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday visited former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who is currently receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN) here.
In a post on X, Ahmad Zahid also prayed for the Bera Member of Parliament’s recovery and continued good health.
“I pray that he will continue to be given strength and good health, that all his affairs will be eased, and that he will be granted a full recovery,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid also prayed that Ismail Sabri would be able to resume his service and daily activities as usual.
Ismail Sabri was reported to have experienced health problems while at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) on Aug 6 for the recording of his statement, before being rushed to IJN.
He subsequently underwent a procedure to implant a wireless pacemaker at the institute to treat an abnormal heart condition. — Bernama

Title: AirBorneo joins FLYsiswa, offers RM400 flight subsidy to eligible students
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 11 — AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd has joined the government-backed FLYsiswa air travel subsidy initiative, offering eligible Malaysian students a RM400 digital voucher to subsidise domestic economy flight tickets, the airline said in a statement today.
According to AirBorneo, the initiative, spearheaded by the Transport Ministry, is aimed at easing travel costs for students studying away from their home states, particularly those travelling between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan.
AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said the cost of air travel should not become an obstacle for students who need to return home during semester breaks, festive periods or emergencies.
“Education requires focus, dedication, and peace of mind. For many young Malaysians studying away from home, particularly between Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo, the cost of flight tickets should never be an obstacle to spending quality time with family,” he said.
He said AirBorneo’s participation in FLYsiswa reflected its commitment to community welfare and would help ease the financial burden on students and their families.
“We look forward to welcoming thousands of students on board our flights, ensuring they enjoy seamless, reliable and affordable travel home,” he said.
The airline said the FLYsiswa initiative is open to eligible Malaysian students enrolled at public universities, polytechnics, community colleges, matriculation colleges and teacher education institutes.
Eligible students can check their status through the Transport Ministry’s FLYsiswa portal and redeem the RM400 digital voucher when booking flights through AirBorneo’s website or mobile application, it said.
The voucher redemption period for AirBorneo flights runs from today until Nov 30, while bookings can be made for travel up to December 31.
AirBorneo said it is also offering additional baggage allowance and complimentary or discounted date-change options for FLYsiswa bookings, subject to its terms and conditions.
The airline said its network would provide students with direct access to key domestic destinations and regional hubs across Sarawak, Sabah and Peninsular Malaysia.

Title: Malaysian detained in India after 4kg of hydroponic cannabis found in luggage
Article:
CHENNAI, Aug 11 — A Malaysian national was detained by Indian authorities after allegedly carrying 4.033 kilogrammes of high-grade hydroponic cannabis through Chennai International Airport, India.
The arrest was made by officers from the Chennai Customs Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) after the suspect arrived from Bangkok on Friday night, based on passenger profiling,
Sinar Harian
reported.
According to the authorities, the suspect was believed to have attempted to leave through the Green Channel without making any declaration to customs.
An X-ray scan of the suspect’s checked luggage detected suspicious images, prompting a detailed inspection.
The inspection uncovered four packages containing a greenish, lumpy substance with a strong and pungent odour.
The packages were believed to contain high-grade hydroponic cannabis concealed in the bottom compartment of the luggage.
The prohibited substance weighed 4,033 grammes and tested positive for cannabis or marijuana using a narcotics detection kit.
Chennai Customs seized the substance under Section 43(a) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985.
The Malaysian suspect was subsequently detained and brought before a court before being remanded in judicial custody.
The case is now being investigated by Indian authorities to identify the network or other parties who may have been involved in the attempt to smuggle the prohibited substance.

Title: Malaysia ready to strengthen defence ties with Iran, says Mohamed Khaled
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 —  Malaysia is ready to expand and strengthen more substantive defence cooperation with Iran based on the close friendship between the two countries.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said this was conveyed during his telephone conversation with Iran’s Acting Minister of Defence and Armed Forces Logistics, Brigadier General Seyed Majid Ebn-e-Reza.
In a Facebook post yesterday, he said Malaysia also hoped that a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on defence cooperation could be finalised as an official instrument to strengthen defence ties between the two countries.
“I also welcomed Iran’s participation in next year’s Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) as a platform to expand relations and explore broader defence cooperation,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled conveyed Malaysia’s condolences over the deaths of Iranian leaders, security personnel and civilians who were killed in the conflict in West Asia.
He said Malaysia hoped a ceasefire could be maintained and that dialogue and diplomatic solutions would continue to be given space in the interest of peace and stability in the region.
He also described Iran as having demonstrated resilience, including through its independently developed defence capabilities.
“Malaysia also appreciates Iran’s cooperation and good treatment in facilitating passage during the conflict. The security of maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, must continue to be safeguarded,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar sues PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim over alleged defamatory remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today filed a defamation suit against PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man over remarks made during a ceramah (political speech) in Pahang last June.
Anwar, as the plaintiff, filed the suit through the law firm S.N. Nair & Partners at the High Court here, naming Tuan Ibrahim as the defendant.
According to the statement of claim, Anwar alleged that the defendant had made defamatory remarks referring to him during a political speech at Felda Jenderak Utara, Kuala Krau, on June 14, in the presence of members of the public and media representatives.
Anwar said a video clip of the speech was subsequently uploaded, published or republished on the YouTube account ‘@Malaysianometry’ the following day (June 15), under the title “Tuan Ibrahim: ‘Pengulas bola direhatkan lepas sertai PAS, ini tanda-tanda PH nak mampus’”.
According to the plaintiff, as of the date the suit was filed, the 11-minute video clip had received more than 20,000 views, 482 likes and 65 comments, and remained accessible, viewable and shareable by the public.—MORE
Anwar said that at 8.08 am on June 15, Tuan Ibrahim himself published a video clip containing the alleged defamatory remarks on his official Facebook account, @Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, while on June 24, the video was also uploaded on the ‘PAS Pahang’ Facebook account.
He alleged that the defamatory words specifically and directly referred to him, his character, integrity, position, profession or status as Prime Minister.
The plaintiff said the defamatory words were untrue, false, baseless, excessive and malicious, and had been uttered or published without any reasonable facts or supporting evidence.
“The plaintiff has never directed, caused, influenced or caused the Royal Malaysia Police to investigate or take action against any individual solely because the individual had criticised the plaintiff, the government or any member of its administration,” the statement of claim said.
Anwar said he had never interfered, directly or indirectly, in determining, selecting, voting for or appointing the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan in the constitutional or customary process relating to the matter in the state.
The plaintiff said that as a result of the defendant’s actions, he had suffered serious damage to his reputation, character, dignity, integrity, credibility, good name and standing, both personally and in his capacities as Prime Minister, Finance Minister, PKR president, Pakatan Harapan chairman and Tambun Member of Parliament.
Anwar therefore sought an injunction to prevent the defendant or his representatives from further publishing or republishing the defamatory words.
The Prime Minister also sought an order requiring the defendant to delete the defamatory publications from any social media accounts, platforms or publications under his possession, custody or control.
In addition to general damages, Anwar is seeking aggravated and exemplary damages, as well as any other relief deemed just and appropriate by the court. — Bernama

Title: Simplified: The Tabung Haji RCI report and what it said
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 11 — Today, in a special sitting of Parliament, MPs are expected to debate a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the country’s Muslim pilgrims’ fund Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Here’s a quick and simplified summary on the 252-page RCI report and some of its key findings:
What is Lembaga Tabung Haji and what is its purpose?
It has two main functions: to administer or manage the fund (which includes the savings by depositors and investments); and to manage all matters regarding pilgrims’ welfare.
The Tabung Haji Act 1995 (Act 535) also enables TH to enter into joint ventures, buy and sell shares, and set up companies if approved by the Religious Affairs Minister.
How big is it?
Currently, TH manages the savings of over 9.8 million depositors.
Based on the latest statistics available on TH’s website, it was managing RM91.747 billion for 9.55 million depositors in 2024.
What is the RCI about?
The RCI was set up to:
investigate Lembaga Tabung Haji’s management and operation issues from 2014 to 2020;
determine if there had been any concealing of information and misleading statements given;
recommend appropriate action for any breaches of law.
When was the RCI conducted and when was its report released?
From its initiation to its completion and its release, the RCI spanned the administration of three prime ministers.
During Bersatu’s Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s time as prime minister, the Cabinet on August 14, 2020 decided there needed to be an RCI, and on July 14, 2021 agreed to set up the RCI and on October 8, 2021 decided on the RCI’s scope of investigations.
On January 20, 2022, the RCI chair, former chief justice Tun Md Raus Sharif and five other RCI members were appointed.
The report dated July 19, 2022 was presented to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on August 30, 2022, and this was when Umno’s Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was prime minister.
The Malaysian government declassified and released the RCI report on July 29 this year, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim explaining that it was not released three years ago as it could have caused depositors to panic and withdraw their savings from TH.
What did the RCI report find and what did it recommend?
1.Tabung Haji’s financial crisis in 2017; TH issued dividends (‘hibah’
) when liabilities exceeded assets
In 2017, TH faced a serious financial crisis as it actually had a RM1.4 billion net loss (instead of the RM3.4 billion net profit recorded in its 2017 financial statement), if accounting standards had been fully complied with.
The RCI said there were five factors that led to the crisis, including TH’s “creative accounting practices” in order to enable it to declare high dividends.
Under the Tabung Haji Act, TH can only declare dividends or distribute profits (hibah) if its assets are more than its liabilities.
But instead of waiting for the audited financial statements and using the asset values there for the years 2014 to 2017, TH used other methods (such as using estimated values via Realisable Asset Value; and tweaking when it should reduce asset values due to impairment losses) in order to have higher asset values for calculations on dividend rates.
The RCI said TH’s dividend or profit distribution (hibah) from 2014 to 2017 did not fulfill the Tabung Haji Act’s controls to ensure depositors are paid from actual profits and not from their own deposits, and the high dividends pre-2018 also caused TH’s reserves to shrink.
Among other things, the RCI said TH’s dividend or distributed profit in 2014 and 2015 exceeded its actual profits for the year, while its liabilities exceeded its assets in 2016 and 2017.
In 2018, the government had to bail out TH in order to close the deficit gap and enable TH to declare dividends for that year, and also to prevent triggering a “bank run” and market instability if TH failed to declare dividends.
This was done through the government’s fully-owned special purpose vehicle Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) using RM19.9 billion to buy over TH’s assets valued at RM9.7 billion.
TH could only pay 1.25 per cent dividend in 2018 when it started fully complying with the accounting standards, but has since been able to issue higher dividends — with the 3.5 per cent declared in 2025 being the highest in eight years.
2. Bonuses too high/unauthorised bonuses
The RCI said TH gave very high bonuses to its employees from 2010 to 2017 (including 2014 to 2017 when audited financial statements showed TH’s liabilities to be higher than its assets), and said this practice should be stopped.
The RCI notes TH had from 2018 started controlling bonus payouts, based on TH’s financial capabilities.
TH’s subsidiary TH Properties Sdn Bhd breached the Companies Act 2016 when giving unauthorised bonuses totalling RM1,148,400 to 14 persons (2017) and RM1.045 million to 10 persons (2018).
The RCI recommends getting back those unauthorised bonuses totalling more than RM2.19 million from TH Properties’ directors and officers.
3. How Tabung Haji’s governance can be improved
The RCI proposed multiple amendments to the Tabung Haji Act (Act 535) to improve TH’s administration.
This includes changing the law to specifically ban active politicians from being directors in TH and its subsidiaries, and to require TH directors to have specific expertise (such as in banking, accounting, economy) instead of only requiring them to be Malaysian Muslims.
4. Investments
Noting suspicious transactions and concealing of information, the RCI proposed a forensic audit on how problematic investment decisions involving 14 companies were made, which caused TH to face severe decline in asset values.
The RCI said TH and its subsidiaries’ directors, management and employees who were involved should be held responsible for these investment losses suffered.
The RCI said TH should focus on fund management portfolios, and should not be involved in high-risk investments (especially what TH classifies as “strategic investments”).
The RCI noted the expansion of TH’s original purposes to also being Muslims’ economic pillar had resulted in its investments in areas where it lacked expertise (such as properties and plantations), resulting in huge losses involving its subsidiaries.
The RCI proposed TH set up a new department (with the proposed name of Dana Haji or Haji fund) to manage investments and to be supervised by the Securities Commission of Malaysia.
5. Policy changes for deposits, pilgrimage payment, pilgrimage subsidies (HAFIS)
The Haj or pilgrimage cost per person has continued to increase from year to year, from just RM15,555 (2003) to RM22,900 (2019) and to RM25,540 (2022), with the RCI saying it is projected to go up to over RM35,000 (2030) and RM50,000 in 2050.
Currently, Malaysian pilgrims do not pay the full Haj cost, as TH has since 2001 been using its investment profits to subsidise up to half or more of the cost.
From 2009 to 2019, first-time pilgrims only had to pay RM9,980 even as the full Haj cost increased annually, while this was increased in 2022 to RM10,980 (paid by B40 pilgrims) and RM12,980 (non-B40 pilgrims).
The RCI said TH’s pilgrimage subsidy or HAFIS bill was projected to continue increasing amid rising costs, which would also affect TH’s profit distribution (hibah) or dividend issued to depositors.
So the RCI proposed TH change its policies:
Minimum deposit for depositors to be eligible for their turn for first Haj: To increase from RM1,300 to the current Haj cost paid by pilgrims (was RM12,980 in 2022) to encourage regular and disciplined savings;
To limit big withdrawals of deposits and require one-month notice before withdrawal;
Give Haj subsidies (HAFIS) only to those who need it; those who can afford should pay full Haj cost.
After the RCI report’s 2026 release, TH on July 30 said it has managed to keep Haj costs at RM33,000 per person for three consecutive years.
What did Tabung Haji say after the release of the RCI report?
Among other things, TH said it has already carried out 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations and is carrying out the others.
TH also said it had, since 2022, only announced dividends based on audited financial statements.
It also said TH is now in a stronger financial position and that it has started to rebuild its reserves.
TH said it has successfully tackled RM12.6 billion in investment losses via the 2018 recovery plan (RM10 billion through UJSB’s asset purchase) and RM2.6 billion in stages up to the end of 2025.
What happened after RCI report’s release?
Following the report’s release, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the police have launched investigations, while the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has also started investigating several individuals after finding discrepancies between their declared income and their assets.

Title: Decades on, Merdeka spirit still burns bright among older Malaysians
Article:
IPOH, Aug 10 — Do you still remember names such as Ali, Siti, Muthu, Jarjit Singh and Ah Meng that often appeared in our primary school textbooks once upon a time?
Those names, once so familiar to earlier generations, seem to bring back memories of friendship, unity and a spirit of togetherness in an independent nation.
That nostalgia was also felt by a group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, as this year’s National Month celebrations took them back to their childhood days and, although decades have passed, memories of celebrating Merdeka (Independence) remain fresh in their minds.
The waving of the Jalur Gemilang and the sound of patriotic songs once again evoked memories of Merdeka celebrations among the group of senior citizens at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak, bringing back the nostalgia etched in their memories.
With great enthusiasm, the senior citizens sang Merdeka-themed songs together, made Jalur Gemilang flags and took part in a flag-assembling game during activities held at the community centre, demonstrating that their love for the country has never faded with age.
For 60-year-old Bhajan Singh, from Gunung Rapat, the activities organised by the community centre are not merely a way to fill his free time, but also an opportunity to reminisce about celebrating National Day during his childhood.
He said the opportunity to get together with his friends from various races also rekindled the spirit of unity that forms the basis of the country’s harmony.
“Although I am getting older, my love for the country remains strong. My memories of celebrating the National Day for the first time are still fresh in my mind, although I was only a child at that time,” he told Bernama recently.
Seventy-five-year-old Jaharah Hashim, from Manong, Kuala Kangsar, said the activities at the centre gave senior citizens the opportunity to forge friendships while putting their minds to the test.
Older Malaysians from various ethnic backgrounds taking part in a batik-themed colouring activity at Halaman Suri Sejahtera Negeri Perak in Taman Lapangan Terbang recently. — Bernama pic
“In the past, we would simply wave the Jalur Gemilang, but now it is more enjoyable because we get to get together with so many friends. Although I am a senior citizen, my enthusiasm for celebrating the National Day has never faded,” she said.
For 64-year-old retired teacher P. Asokan, from Lahat here, the activities were truly meaningful as they brought together people from different ethnic backgrounds to appreciate the meaning of Merdeka.
“When I come here, I see Malays, Chinese and Indians all enthusiastically celebrating the National Day. This is the spirit that must continue to be nurtured so that we always appreciate the blessings of independence and national unity,” he said.
Meanwhile, programme coordinator Nur Hayatulasna Mohamed Fishal said the National Day-themed programme was held for the first time at the community centre as an effort to foster the spirit of patriotism among senior citizens.
She said various activities had been organised, including singing patriotic songs, making Jalur Gemilang flags with Pos Malaysia and a flag-assembling game.
“Although it was held on a small scale, we hope this programme can inspire the spirit of Merdeka among the participants and strengthen ties within the community.
“Their age is advancing, and their strength may have diminished, but their gratitude for the blessings of independence and love for the country remain unwavering, proving that patriotism knows no age,” she said.
‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’ (Malaysia Madani: Shared Prosperity), which has been selected as the theme for the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM 2026) celebrations, among other things, emphasises that the country’s prosperity should be enjoyed fairly and comprehensively by everyone for the sake of shared harmony. — Bernama
